title.zh: 卷402 列傳一百八十九 乌兰泰 长瑞 长寿 董光甲 邵鹤龄 邓绍良 石玉龙 周天受弟：天培 天孚 饶廷选 文瑞 彭斯举 张玉良 鲁占鳌 刘季三 双来 瞿腾龙 王国才 虎坤元 戴文英
title.en: Volume 402 Biographies 189: Wu Lantai, Zhang Rui, Chang Shou, Dong Guangjia, Shao Heling, Deng Shaoliang, Shi Yulong, Zhou Tianshou younger brother: Tian Pei, Tian Fu, Rao Tingxuan, Wen Rui, Peng Siju, Zhang Yuliang, Lu Zhanao, Liu Jisan, Shuang Lai, Qu Tenglong, Wang Guocai, Hu Kun Yuan, Dai Wenying
title.raw: 卷402 列傳一百八十九 乌兰泰 长瑞 长寿 董光甲 邵鹤龄 邓绍良 石玉龙 周天受弟：天培 天孚 饶廷选 文瑞 彭斯举 张玉良 鲁占鳌 刘季三 双来 瞿腾龙 王国才 虎坤元 戴文英

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰，字遠芳，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai, courtesy name Yuanfang, was a man of the Plain Red Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai, whose courtesy name was Yuanfang, came from the Plain Red Banner of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 由火器營鳥槍護軍從征回疆有功，升藍翎長，累擢護軍參領、營總、翼長。

translations.literal: Starting as a musket guard in the Firearms Brigade, he campaigned in Xinjiang with merit, was promoted to Blue Feather Chief, and was repeatedly advanced to guard deputy commander, battalion commander, and wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a musket guard in the Firearms Brigade; service in the Xinjiang campaigns earned him promotion to Blue Feather Chief, and he rose in turn to guard deputy commander, battalion commander, and wing commander.

sentences.zh: 軍政卓異，道光二十七年，擢廣東副都統。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding in the military administration review, in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he was promoted to vice commander of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Marked out as outstanding in the military administration review, he was appointed vice commander of Guangdong in the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign (1847).

sentences.zh: 善訓練，講求火器。

translations.literal: He was skilled at training troops and devoted attention to firearms.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at drill and took special care with firearms.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，廣西匪熾，詔烏蘭泰幫辨軍務，選帶適用器械及得力章京兵丁赴軍，以廣東綠營精兵五百人隸之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, banditry flared in Guangxi; the throne ordered Wu Lantai to assist in military affairs, to select suitable weapons and capable clerks and soldiers for the campaign, and five hundred elite Guangdong Green Standard troops were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry surged in Guangxi in the first year of Xianfeng (1851), the court ordered Wu Lantai to help manage the war effort. He was to bring useful arms and capable staff and troops to the front, with five hundred picked Guangdong Green Standard soldiers assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 四月，偕向榮、秦定三等圍賊於武宣，賊竄象州，自請治罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, together with Xiang Rong and Qin Dingsan he besieged the rebels at Wuxuan; the rebels fled to Xiangzhou, and he asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he joined Xiang Rong and Qin Dingsan in besieging the rebels at Wuxuan, but the rebels broke out toward Xiangzhou, and Wu Lantai asked that he himself be punished.

sentences.zh: 詔以其初至，免議，命偕向榮節制鎮將。

translations.literal: An edict, on the ground that he had only just arrived, exempted him from inquiry and ordered him to join Xiang Rong in commanding the regional generals.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had only just reached the front, the court declined to pursue the matter and instructed him to work with Xiang Rong in directing the regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 時軍中將帥不和，文宗憂之，密諭烏蘭泰實陳勿隱。

translations.literal: At the time the army's commanders were at odds; Emperor Wenzong was troubled and secretly instructed Wu Lantai to report the facts frankly and conceal nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Discord among the commanders worried Emperor Wenzong, who secretly told Wu Lantai to speak plainly and withhold nothing.

sentences.zh: 上疏略曰：「週天爵奏向榮曲徇其子，致失眾心，不為無因。

translations.literal: He memorialized in summary: "Zhou Tianjue's memorial that Xiang Rong bent the rules for his son and thereby lost the troops' hearts is not without cause.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, in part: "Zhou Tianjue charged that Xiang Rong showed favor to his son and lost the army's confidence; that complaint was not groundless.

sentences.zh: 武宣之役，秦定三、周鳳岐、張敬修連營防禦，其堵剿不利，追賊遲延，咎當同任。

translations.literal: In the Wuxuan campaign, Qin Dingsan, Zhou Fengqi, and Zhang Jingxiu held successive camps on the defensive; their blocking and pursuit went poorly and the pursuit of the rebels was delayed—the blame should be shared.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxuan, Qin Dingsan, Zhou Fengqi, and Zhang Jingxiu had lined up camp after camp on the defensive; their blocking actions failed and the pursuit lagged, and responsibility ought to fall on all of them alike.

sentences.zh: 天爵劾定三、鳳岐，不及敬修，人心不服。

translations.literal: Tianjue impeached Dingsan and Fengqi but not Jingxiu, and men's minds were not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue had impeached Dingsan and Fengqi but not Jingxiu, which left the troops unconvinced.

sentences.zh: 向榮將官傅春、和春失利，天爵責定三不並力，後訪知實非退縮，諉為向榮推卸之言。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong's officers Fu Chun and He Chun suffered defeat; Tianjue blamed Dingsan for not joining forces, but later investigation showed there had in fact been no shrinking back—it was language by which Xiang Rong shifted blame.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Rong's subordinates Fu Chun and He Chun were beaten, Tianjue blamed Dingsan for failing to cooperate; inquiry later showed there had been no real retreat, only words by which Xiang Rong shifted the blame.

sentences.zh: 因之天爵、榮、定三皆有隙。

translations.literal: Because of this, Tianjue, Rong, and Dingsan all bore grudges against one another.
translations.idiomatic: From this sprang mutual ill will among Tianjue, Xiang Rong, and Dingsan.

sentences.zh: 天爵年老，直強、耳輭，其子光岳干預，致失人心。」

translations.literal: Tianjue was old, blunt and stiff yet soft-eared; his son Guangyue meddled, and thus he lost men's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue was elderly, obstinate yet easily swayed; his son Guangyue interfered in affairs, and he too lost the army's trust."

sentences.zh: 又言：「向榮初勦賊屢捷，未免輕賊。

translations.literal: He also said: "At first, in suppressing the rebels, Xiang Rong won repeated victories and could not help but underestimate the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In the early campaigns Xiang Rong won victory after victory and came to underestimate the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及其子招嫌，楚兵藉口，遂多諉卸。

translations.literal: When his son drew suspicion, the Hunan troops took it as a pretext, and thereupon he often shifted blame.
translations.idiomatic: Once his son became a source of resentment, the Hunan soldiers used it as an excuse, and he began to pass blame to others far more often.

sentences.zh: 然在軍鎮將無及榮者。

translations.literal: Yet among the regional generals in the army none matched Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, among the regional commanders in the field none equaled Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 更易其兵，仍可立功。」

translations.literal: If his troops were replaced, he could still achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: Replace his troops and he could still win distinction."

sentences.zh: 上下其疏，命賽尚阿覈奏，賽尚阿請不咎既往，令烏蘭泰與向榮分任軍事，以專責成。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent up and down; Sai Shang'a was ordered to verify and report; Sai Shang'a asked that past faults not be punished and that Wu Lantai and Xiang Rong divide military duties so that each might bear focused responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The court circulated his memorial and ordered Sai Shang'a to investigate. Sai Shang'a recommended letting bygones be bygones and dividing command between Wu Lantai and Xiang Rong so that each could be held to a clear account.

sentences.zh: 賊踞象州中坪，烏蘭泰督貴州三鎮兵，由羅秀進梁山村，逼近賊巢。

translations.literal: The rebels held Zhongping in Xiangzhou; Wu Lantai directed the troops of Guizhou's three commands, advanced from Luoxiu toward Liangshan village, and drew near the rebel stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were entrenched at Zhongping in Xiangzhou. Wu Lantai led the forces of Guizhou's three regional commands from Luoxiu toward Liangshan village and closed on their lair.

sentences.zh: 賊乘駐營未定，猛撲，連擊敗之，殪賊千餘。

translations.literal: The rebels, seizing the moment before the camp was settled, struck fiercely; he repeatedly defeated them and killed more than a thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rushed him while his camp was still unsettled, but he beat them back again and again and killed more than a thousand of them.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，賊竄桂平新墟，烏蘭泰分四路進攻，破伏賊於莫村，一日七戰皆捷，斬級數千，賜花翎。

translations.literal: That autumn the rebels fled to Xinxu in Guiping; Wu Lantai attacked along four routes, broke ambushing rebels at Mo village, fought seven battles in one day—all victories—and beheaded several thousand; he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the rebels withdrew to Xinxu in Guiping. Wu Lantai advanced on four fronts, routed an ambush at Mo village, and fought seven engagements in a single day, winning every one and taking several thousand heads. The court awarded him the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 賊屯紫荊山，新墟為山前門戶，雙髻山、豬仔峽為山後要隘，負隅死拒。

translations.literal: The rebels encamped on Zijing Mountain; Xinxu was the mountain's forward gateway, Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge were vital passes to the rear, and they defended to the death from a cornered position.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zijing Mountain, with Xinxu as the gateway before it and Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge as the key passes behind; they fought from their stronghold as if they had no way out.

sentences.zh: 向榮偕巴清德連奪雙髻山、豬仔峽，合攻風門坳，破之。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong, together with Ba Qingde, successively seized Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge, joined in attacking Fengmen'ao, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong and Ba Qingde took Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge in succession, then joined in storming Fengmen'ao and carried it.

sentences.zh: 進逼新墟，迭攻不下，其附近村落掃蕩幾盡。

translations.literal: Pressing on Xinxu, they attacked again and again without taking it; the nearby villages were swept almost clean.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed toward Xinxu but failed to take it despite repeated assaults, though the surrounding villages were nearly cleared out.

sentences.zh: 閏八月，賊編木牌欲渡河，烏蘭泰迭擊，大敗之，詔嘉獎，加都統銜。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month the rebels lashed together wooden rafts intending to cross the river; Wu Lantai struck them repeatedly and inflicted a great defeat; an edict praised him and added the rank insignia of commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the rebels built rafts to cross the river; Wu Lantai attacked them again and again and routed them completely. The throne commended him and promoted him to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 於是賊棄新墟他竄，向榮等追至平南，敗績，賊遂陷永安州。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebels abandoned Xinxu and fled elsewhere; Xiang Rong and others pursued to Pingnan, suffered defeat, and the rebels thereupon took Yong'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then abandoned Xinxu and broke away. Xiang Rong pursued as far as Pingnan but was beaten, and the rebels went on to seize Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰追至，戰於水竇、圞嶺，皆大捷，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai pursued to the scene and fought at Shuidou and Tuanling—both great victories—and was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai followed up and fought at Shuidou and Tuanling, winning decisive victories in both places. He was given the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 永安地險，賊皆死黨固結，僅烏蘭泰一軍久戰已疲，故不能制之。

translations.literal: Yong'an's terrain was perilous; the rebels were all diehards firmly united; only Wu Lantai's single army had fought long and was already weary—hence they could not be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an was difficult country, and the rebels were fanatically loyal and tightly knit. Wu Lantai alone had borne the brunt for so long that his troops were exhausted, and for that reason the enemy could not be brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 向榮自平南敗後被譴，託病逗留梧州、平樂者兩月有餘。

translations.literal: After his defeat at Pingnan, Xiang Rong was censured; pleading illness, he lingered at Wuzhou and Pingle for more than two months.
translations.idiomatic: Censured after his defeat at Pingnan, Xiang Rong claimed illness and remained at Wuzhou and Pingle for more than two months.

sentences.zh: 至冬始抵永安，攻北路，烏蘭泰攻南路，毀水竇賊巢。

translations.literal: Only when winter came did he reach Yong'an; he attacked the northern route while Wu Lantai attacked the southern route and destroyed the rebel nest at Shuidou.
translations.idiomatic: He did not reach Yong'an until winter, when he took the northern line while Wu Lantai attacked from the south and destroyed the rebel base at Shuidou.

sentences.zh: 向榮亦進奪槓嶺要隘，合擊迭挫賊。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong also advanced and seized the vital pass at Gangling; in combined attacks they repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong also pushed forward and took the strategic pass at Gangling; fighting together, the two commanders drove the rebels back again and again.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿親蒞督戰，期在必克。

translations.literal: Sai Shang'a came in person to supervise the fighting, with the expectation of certain capture.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a came to the front in person to direct operations, determined that the city must fall.

sentences.zh: 江忠源號知兵，隸烏蘭泰軍，倚其贊助；

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan was famed as knowing warfare; he served under Wu Lantai's army, who relied on his assistance;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan, renowned as a soldier of real ability, served under Wu Lantai, who leaned heavily on his counsel;

sentences.zh: 每言賊凶悍，久蔓將不可製，必聚而殲之。

translations.literal: he often said the rebels were fierce, that if allowed to spread long they would become uncontrollable, and that they must be gathered together and annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: and he kept warning that the rebels were savage fighters, that if the revolt were allowed to spread it would soon be beyond control, and that the enemy must be cornered and destroyed in one blow.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰主鎖圍困賊，向榮謂圍城缺一面，乃古法，宜縱賊出擊，兩人意不合。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai favored a tight encirclement to trap the rebels; Xiang Rong said that leaving one side of a siege open was the ancient method and that the rebels should be allowed out to be struck—the two men's views did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai wanted a complete encirclement, but Xiang Rong argued that leaving one side open was the classical way to besiege a city and that the rebels should be let out and then struck down. The two men could not agree.

sentences.zh: 會榮克城西砲台，二年元旦，同詣賽尚阿賀歲。

translations.literal: When Rong captured the western batteries of the city, on New Year's Day of the second year they both went to congratulate Sai Shang'a.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang Rong took the western batteries, both commanders called on Sai Shang'a on New Year's Day of the second year to offer their greetings.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿遇榮特優，烏蘭泰憤甚，忠源解之，然益不相能。

translations.literal: Sai Shang'a treated Rong with special favor; Wu Lantai was deeply angered; Zhongyuan tried to smooth things over, yet they became even less able to work together.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a showed Xiang Rong conspicuous favor, which infuriated Wu Lantai. Jiang Zhongyuan tried to mediate, but the two commanders grew even more hostile to each other.

sentences.zh: 忠源以母憂，辭歸。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan, on account of his mother's death, resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan then left the army to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 時嚴詔促戰，春雨連旬，士卒疲困。

translations.literal: At the time stern edicts urged battle; spring rain fell for successive ten-day periods; officers and men were weary and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Strict orders from the court pressed for action, but spring rains lasted for weeks and the troops were worn down.

sentences.zh: 二月，賊棄城冒雨夜走，北犯桂林。

translations.literal: In the second month the rebels abandoned the city, stole away by night in the rain, and marched north against Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the rebels evacuated the city and slipped away north through the rain toward Guilin.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰率兵急追至昭平山中，路險雨滑，為賊所乘，敗績，總兵長瑞、長壽、董光甲、邵鶴齡死之。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai led troops in hot pursuit into the mountains of Zhaoping; the roads were perilous and rain made them slippery; the rebels seized the advantage; there was a defeat; regional commanders Chang Rui, Chang Shou, Dong Guangjia, and Shao Heling died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai hurried after them into the Zhaoping hills, where treacherous paths and rain-slick ground let the rebels turn on him. His force was shattered, and the regional commanders Chang Rui, Chang Shou, Dong Guangjia, and Shao Heling were killed.

sentences.zh: 向榮徑收州城，由間道趨桂林，先賊至。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong went straight to recover the prefectural city, took a bypath toward Guilin, and arrived before the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong marched straight to reoccupy the prefectural seat, took a side road to Guilin, and reached the city ahead of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰踵賊後，戰於南門外，爭將軍橋，砲中右腿，創甚，退屯陽朔，越二十日卒於軍。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai followed on the rebels' heels, fought outside the south gate, contested Jiangjun Bridge, was struck in the right leg by cannon fire, was gravely wounded, withdrew to camp at Yangshuo, and after more than twenty days died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai came up behind the rebels and fought outside the south gate for control of Jiangjun Bridge. A cannon ball struck his right leg and left him badly wounded. He fell back to Yangshuo and died in camp twenty days later.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰忠勇為諸將冠，文宗深惜之，賜銀一千兩治喪，予輕車都尉世職，諡武壯。

translations.literal: Wu Lantai's loyalty and courage stood first among the generals; Emperor Wenzong deeply regretted his loss, granted a thousand taels of silver for the funeral, bestowed the hereditary office of Commandant of Light Chariots, and gave the posthumous title Wuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lantai's loyalty and valor had been unmatched among the commanders. Emperor Wenzong mourned him deeply, granted a thousand taels of silver for his funeral, conferred the hereditary rank of Commandant of Light Chariots, and posthumously titled him Wuzhuang (Stalwart in War).

sentences.zh: 長瑞、長壽，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Chang Rui and Chang Shou were of the Guwalgiya clan, men of the Plain White Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rui and Chang Shou belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from the Plain White Banner of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 父塔思哈，道光初，官喀什噶爾幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Their father Tasiha, in the early Daoguang period, served as assistant minister at Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Tasiha had served in the early Daoguang era as assistant minister at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 叛回張格爾作亂，殉難，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When the rebel Muslim Zhang Ge'er rose in revolt, he died for the state; a hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslim rebel Zhang Ge'er rose in revolt, Tasiha died in the fighting, and his family received the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 長瑞襲世職，授三等侍衛，累擢直隸天津鎮總兵；

translations.literal: Chang Rui inherited the hereditary office, was appointed third-rank imperial bodyguard, and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Zhili's Tianjin garrison;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rui inherited the family rank, was made a third-rank imperial bodyguard, and rose in time to regional commander of the Tianjin garrison in Zhili;

sentences.zh: 長壽以廕授藍翎侍衛，累擢甘肅涼州鎮總兵：並從賽尚阿赴廣西剿匪，同領湖南兵。

translations.literal: Chang Shou, by yin privilege, was appointed a Blue Feather bodyguard, and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Gansu's Liangzhou garrison: both followed Sai Shang'a to Guangxi to suppress bandits and jointly led Hunan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shou entered service by yin privilege as a Blue Feather bodyguard and eventually became regional commander of the Liangzhou garrison in Gansu. Both brothers followed Sai Shang'a to Guangxi and commanded Hunan troops together.

sentences.zh: 長瑞戰風門坳有功，新墟禦賊失利，奪職留營。

translations.literal: Chang Rui had merit fighting at Fengmen'ao; in defending Xinxu against the rebels he suffered defeat, was stripped of office but kept at camp.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rui distinguished himself at Fengmen'ao but was defeated defending Xinxu; he was dismissed from his post yet kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 及賊由永安出竄，從烏蘭泰躡追至龍寮嶺，地險，左右止勿進。

translations.literal: When the rebels broke out from Yong'an, he followed Wu Lantai in pursuit to Longliao Ridge; the ground was perilous, and those on his left and right urged him not to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels broke out of Yong'an, he followed Wu Lantai in pursuit to Longliao Ridge. The terrain was treacherous, and his officers begged him to halt.

sentences.zh: 長瑞曰：「軍令孰敢違者！

translations.literal: Chang Rui said: "Who would dare disobey a military order!
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rui replied, "Who would dare disobey an order from headquarters?

sentences.zh: 死耳，勿復言。」

translations.literal: Death—that is all; speak no more."
translations.idiomatic: We die, that is all—say no more."

sentences.zh: 以母老，令長壽毋相從，長壽泣曰：「貪生忘國，非孝也。」

translations.literal: Because their mother was old, he ordered Chang Shou not to accompany him; Chang Shou wept and said: "To cling to life and forget one's country is not filial."
translations.idiomatic: Their mother was elderly, and Chang Rui told Chang Shou to stay behind. Chang Shou wept and said, "To cling to life and forget one's country is not filial piety."

sentences.zh: 卒偕行。

translations.literal: In the end he went along.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he went with his brother.

sentences.zh: 值大霧，賊以巨砲扼山間。

translations.literal: A heavy fog set in; the rebels used great cannon to hold the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: A thick fog descended, and the rebels blocked the mountain defiles with heavy guns.

sentences.zh: 軍士兩日不得食，為賊衝潰踐踏，死無算。

translations.literal: The soldiers had gone two days without food; the rebels charged, broke them, and trampled them; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had not eaten for two days. The rebel charge broke their ranks, and men were trampled underfoot until the dead could not be counted.

sentences.zh: 長壽墜馬，長瑞挺矛救之，身被數十創，同遇害。

translations.literal: Chang Shou fell from his horse; Chang Rui thrust with his spear to rescue him, received several dozen wounds on his body, and both met their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shou was thrown from his horse. Chang Rui spurred forward with his spear to save him, took dozens of wounds, and both brothers were killed.

sentences.zh: 文宗以其父子​​兄弟皆死難，深惜之，並贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, because father, sons, and brothers all died for the state, deeply regretted them, posthumously promoted both to provincial commander-in-chief, and granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant combined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong mourned a family in which father, sons, and brothers had all died for the dynasty. He posthumously promoted both brothers to provincial commander-in-chief and granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 存問其母，賜銀三百兩。

translations.literal: He sent inquiries after their mother and granted three hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He sent condolences to their mother and granted her three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 長瑞諡武壯，長壽諡勤勇，於永安建祠曰雙忠，同死者附祀焉。

translations.literal: Chang Rui was posthumously titled Wuzhuang, Chang Shou Qinyong; at Yong'an a shrine called Shuangzhong (Twin Loyalty) was built, and those who died with them were attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rui received the posthumous title Wuzhuang and Chang Shou the title Qinyong (Diligent and Brave). A shrine called Twin Loyalty was raised at Yong'an, with the others who fell that day enshrined beside them.

sentences.zh: 董光甲，直隸河間人。

translations.literal: Dong Guangjia was a native of Hejian in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Guangjia came from Hejian in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十四年武進士，授守備。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took the military jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiaqing (1809) and was appointed garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累擢河南河北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Henan's Hebei garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to regional commander of the Hebei garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 從向榮攻永安，奪槓嶺、摩天嶺、天鵝嶺諸要隘。

translations.literal: Following Xiang Rong in the attack on Yong'an, he seized the vital passes at Gangling, Motian Ridge, and Tian'e Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Xiang Rong at Yong'an, he took the strategic passes at Gangling, Motian Ridge, and Tian'e Ridge.

sentences.zh: 追賊至昭平，迭擊賊於古束、龍寮嶺，次黃茆嶺。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels to Zhaoping, he repeatedly struck them at Gushu and Longliao Ridge, and next at Huangmao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels to Zhaoping and fought them in succession at Gushu, Longliao Ridge, and then Huangmao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊反撲，力戰死之，贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡勇烈。

translations.literal: The rebels counterattacked; he fought fiercely and died; he was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous title Yonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels turned on him, he fought to the death. He was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and titled Yonglie (Fierce and Upright).

sentences.zh: 邵鶴齡，山東招遠人。

translations.literal: Shao Heling was a native of Zhaoyuan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Heling came from Zhaoyuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he passed the civil jinshi examination and was appointed third-rank imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing (1820) and was made a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累擢湖北鄖陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Hubei's Yunyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became regional commander of the Yunyang garrison in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 偕長瑞等同追賊龍寮嶺，殞於陣，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡威確。

translations.literal: Together with Chang Rui and others he pursued the rebels to Longliao Ridge, fell in battle, was granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous title Weique.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Chang Rui in the pursuit to Longliao Ridge and was killed in action. He received the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Commandant and the posthumous title Weique (Formidable and Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 鄧紹良，字臣若，湖南乾州廳人。

translations.literal: Deng Shaoliang, courtesy name Chenruo, was a native of Qianzhou subprefecture in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shaoliang, whose courtesy name was Chenruo, came from Qianzhou subprefecture in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 由屯弁累擢守備。

translations.literal: From a garrison squad leader he was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a garrison squad leader and rose step by step to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從剿崇陽土匪李沅發，率五百人破賊金峰嶺，擒沅發，擢都司，賜花翎、揚勇巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: In suppressing the Chongyang bandit Li Yuanfa, he led five hundred men to defeat the rebels at Jinfeng Ridge, captured Yuanfa, was promoted to battalion vice-commander, and was granted the peacock feather and the title of Baturu, Exalter of Valor.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the Chongyang bandit Li Yuanfa, he led five hundred men to break the rebels at Jinfeng Ridge and capture Li himself. He was promoted to battalion vice-commander and given the peacock feather and the honorific Baturu, Exalter of Valor.

sentences.zh: 遂從向榮赴廣西勦賊，潯州牛排嶺之戰，以精騎張左右翼，擊兩路賊，皆挫之。

translations.literal: He then followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi to suppress rebels; in the battle at Niupaiziling in Xunzhou, with elite cavalry he spread the left and right wings, struck two columns of rebels, and defeated both.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi. At Niupaiziling in Xunzhou he deployed elite cavalry on both flanks and drove back two rebel columns.

sentences.zh: 又戰象州、永安州，皆有功。

translations.literal: He also fought at Xiangzhou and Yong'an prefecture, with merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Xiangzhou and Yong'an and distinguished himself in both places.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，授楚雄協副將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed deputy regional commander of the Chuxiong command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he was appointed deputy commander of the Chuxiong garrison.

sentences.zh: 二年，援桂林，屯西門，力戰卻賊。

translations.literal: In the second year he relieved Guilin, encamped at the west gate, fought fiercely and repelled the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he marched to relieve Guilin, held the west gate, and beat the rebels back in heavy fighting.

sentences.zh: 追賊入湖南，援長沙，入任城守，地雷發，持刀屹立，砲洞左臂，不動，殪先登賊，賊退，城复完，軍中稱其勇。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Hunan, he relieved Changsha, entered to take charge of the city's defense; a land mine exploded; he stood with saber drawn unmoved; a cannon ball pierced his left arm—he did not stir; he killed the first rebels to scale the wall; the rebels withdrew; the city was made whole again; the army praised his courage.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the rebels into Hunan and helped relieve Changsha, where he took charge of the defense. When a mine exploded he stood his ground with saber in hand; a cannon ball tore his left arm, yet he did not budge, cut down the first rebels over the wall, and drove the enemy back until the city was secure. The army acclaimed his valor.

sentences.zh: 洎賊解圍竄湖北，巴陵土匪晏仲武勾結肆掠，紹良偕總兵阿勒經阿剿平之。

translations.literal: When the rebels lifted the siege and fled to Hubei, the Baling bandit Yan Zhongwu colluded in widespread plunder; Shaoliang, together with regional commander Alejing'a, suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels raised the siege and withdrew into Hubei, the Baling bandit Yan Zhongwu joined in widespread looting. Deng Shaoliang and the regional commander Alejing'a crushed the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢安徽壽春鎮總兵，詔率所部從向榮援江南，廷臣多薦紹良者，尋擢江南提督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to regional commander of Anhui's Shouchun garrison; an edict ordered him to lead his troops with Xiang Rong to relieve Jiangnan; many court officials recommended Shaoliang; soon he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made regional commander of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui and ordered to bring his troops with Xiang Rong to the Jiangnan front. Many officials at court spoke for him, and he was soon appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 榮令分剿鎮江踞賊，進擊觀音山，合攻瓜洲，皆捷。

translations.literal: Rong ordered him to divide forces and suppress the rebels holding Zhenjiang, advance against Guanyin Mountain, and join in attacking Guazhou—all victories.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent him to clear rebels from Zhenjiang, attack Guanyin Mountain, and join the assault on Guazhou. He won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 逼城而軍，賊設伏北固山下，而自城突出撲營，火四起，官軍不能禦。

translations.literal: Pressing the army close to the city, the rebels set an ambush below Beigu Mountain while bursting out from the city to strike the camp; fires rose on every side; the government troops could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed close to the city walls, but the rebels ambushed his force below Beigu Mountain and sallied from the city to overrun the camp. Fires broke out everywhere, and the government troops could not hold.

sentences.zh: 退守丹陽，褫職議罪，仍隸向榮軍，帶罪自效。

translations.literal: He withdrew to defend Danyang, was stripped of office and subject to punishment, yet remained under Xiang Rong's army to redeem his fault through service.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Danyang, was dismissed and marked for punishment, but remained with Xiang Rong's army to redeem himself in the field.

sentences.zh: 賊兩次窺伺東壩，榮令紹良擊走之。

translations.literal: The rebels twice probed Dongba; Rong ordered Shaoliang to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels twice tested Dongba, Xiang Rong sent Deng Shaoliang to drive them away.

sentences.zh: 四年，克太平，紹良移軍駐守，又破賊採石。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Taiping was taken; Shaoliang moved his army to garrison it and again defeated the rebels at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Taiping fell. Deng Shaoliang garrisoned the city and then defeated the rebels at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 向榮疏陳戰功，為乞免罪，允之。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong memorialized his battle achievements and asked that his punishment be remitted; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong memorialized his victories and asked that his punishment be set aside; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時賊由蕪湖窺徽州、寧國，紹良屯黃池，賊酋石國宗糾各路賊萬餘來犯。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels from Wuhu were watching Huizhou and Ningguo; Shaoliang encamped at Huangchi; the rebel chief Shi Guozong gathered more than ten thousand from various routes to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Wuhu were threatening Huizhou and Ningguo. Deng Shaoliang held Huangchi when the rebel leader Shi Guozong mustered more than ten thousand men from several bands and attacked.

sentences.zh: 紹良兵少，設伏山溝，多張疑兵，誘賊入，痛殲之。

translations.literal: Shaoliang's troops were few; he set an ambush in a mountain ravine, deployed many decoy forces, lured the rebels in, and annihilated them painfully.
translations.idiomatic: Though his force was small, he laid an ambush in a mountain gorge, spread decoys widely, drew the rebels in, and cut them to pieces.

sentences.zh: 五年春，賊复乘夜撲營。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the rebels again stormed the camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the rebels again rushed his camp by night.

sentences.zh: 伏槍砲，俟近驟發，殲賊無算。

translations.literal: He placed muskets and cannon in ambush; when the enemy drew near he opened fire suddenly and destroyed rebels beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He hid muskets and cannon, waited until they were close, and opened fire without warning, killing rebels beyond number.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉紹良力遏賊鋒，保全甚大，予三品頂戴，复花翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised Shaoliang for forcefully checking the rebels' spearhead and achieving great preservation, granted him the third-rank official's button, and restored the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised him for bluntly checking the rebel advance and saving the region from great harm, gave him the third-rank official's button, and restored his peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 賊既退歸，复圖襲徽、寧，以窺浙境。

translations.literal: After the rebels had withdrawn, they again plotted to strike Huizhou and Ningguo in order to spy out the Zhejiang border.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew they soon turned again toward Huizhou and Ningguo, probing toward Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 紹良奉命馳往，統各路援兵，至則簡精銳，伏要隘伺擊，屢破賊，克婺源、黟、石埭諸縣，复提督銜。

translations.literal: Shaoliang was ordered to hurry there, took command of relief troops from all routes, and upon arrival selected elite troops, lay in ambush at vital passes to await and strike, repeatedly defeated the rebels, recovered the counties of Wuyuan, Yi, and Shidi, and was restored to provincial commander-in-chief rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to the scene at once, he took command of reinforcements from every direction, picked elite troops on arrival, and ambushed the rebels at key passes. He won repeated victories, recovered Wuyuan, Yi, and Shidi, and was restored to provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊聚於蕪湖，窺南陵、黃池。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered at Wuhu and watched Nanling and Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed at Wuhu and threatened Nanling and Huangchi.

sentences.zh: 紹良由灣沚進剿，連破賊，焚其舟，遂剋蕪湖，授陝西提督。

translations.literal: Shaoliang advanced from Wanzhi to suppress them, repeatedly defeated the rebels, burned their boats, thereupon took Wuhu, and was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shaoliang advanced from Wanzhi, defeated them in a series of engagements, burned their boats, and took Wuhu. He was then appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 六年春，江寧賊上竄，踞倉頭鎮，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the Jiangning rebels fled upward, occupied Cangtou town, and their momentum was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year rebels from Nanjing broke north and seized Cangtou town with great force.

sentences.zh: 向榮令紹良往督戰，而諸將意不愜，轉不盡力，於是戰不利，紹良受傷，坐褫花翎。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered Shaoliang to go and supervise the fighting, but the various generals were displeased and in turn did not exert themselves fully; thus the battle went poorly; Shaoliang was wounded; he was punished by stripping the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent Deng Shaoliang to direct the fighting, but the other generals resented the assignment and held back. The battle went badly, Shaoliang was wounded, and he lost his peacock feather as punishment.

sentences.zh: 德興阿軍潰，揚州陷。

translations.literal: Degxing'a's army collapsed; Yangzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Degxing'a's army broke, and Yangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 詔紹良渡江赴援，幫辦江北軍務。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shaoliang to cross the river to go to the relief and to assist in managing northern Jiang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commanded Shaoliang to cross the Yangtze and join the relief effort, with responsibility for assisting in northern Jiang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 破藥王廟賊壘，環攻揚州六晝夜，克之，又追破賊於三汊河。

translations.literal: He destroyed the rebel fort at the Medicine King Temple, besieged Yangzhou for six days and six nights, took it, and again pursued and defeated the rebels at San Cha River.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the rebel stronghold at the Medicine King Temple, laid siege to Yangzhou for six days and nights until it fell, then pursued and routed the rebels at San Cha River.

sentences.zh: 會寧國告陷，復命幫辦皖南軍務。

translations.literal: When it was reported that Ningguo had fallen, he was again ordered to assist in managing southern Anhui military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived that Ningguo had fallen, he was reassigned to assist in the defense of southern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 移軍赴援，扼金河橋，大破賊於東溪橋，又迭擊賊於涇縣，挫之，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: He moved his army to go to the relief, held Jinhe Bridge, greatly defeated the rebels at Dongxi Bridge, and again repeatedly struck the rebels at Jing County, thwarting them; he was transferred to Zhejiang provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the rescue, seized Jinhe Bridge, and inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebels at Dongxi Bridge. After a series of engagements at Jing County that checked the enemy advance, he was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 賊糾黨數万來援，敗之於楊柳鋪。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered allies numbering tens of thousands to come to the relief; he defeated them at Yangliu Post.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels mustered tens of thousands to reinforce the enemy, he defeated them at Yangliu Post.

sentences.zh: 副將周天受遇賊夏家渡，戰未利。

translations.literal: Vice General Zhou Tianshou encountered the rebels at Xiajia Ferry; the battle was not favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Zhou Tianshou clashed with the rebels at Xiajia Ferry, but the engagement went poorly.

sentences.zh: 紹良乘隙縱擊，賊大潰，遂督諸軍連奪夏家渡、團山諸賊壘，破七里岡賊巢，進攻寧國，十二月，克之。

translations.literal: Shaoliang seized the opening and unleashed an attack; the rebels were greatly routed. He then supervised the various armies in continuously taking Xiajia Ferry, Tuanshan, and other rebel forts, destroyed the rebel nest at Qiligang, advanced to attack Ningguo, and in the twelfth month took it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang seized the opening and launched a fierce assault, sending the rebels into full rout. Leading the combined forces, he captured Xiajia Ferry, Tuanshan, and other rebel positions in succession, destroyed the stronghold at Qiligang, and besieged Ningguo — which fell in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁母憂，奪情留軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he entered mourning for his mother; his leave of mourning was set aside and he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng, upon his mother's death he was granted leave to mourn, yet the throne required him to remain at his post with the army.

sentences.zh: 紹良以寧國為浙之屏蔽，而涇縣為咽喉要衝，屯軍扼之，賊屢犯不得逞。

translations.literal: Shaoliang regarded Ningguo as Zhejiang's shield and Jing County as the vital throat passage; he stationed troops to hold them, and though the rebels repeatedly attacked, they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang held that Ningguo shielded Zhejiang while Jing County guarded the crucial pass; by garrisoning troops there he foiled repeated rebel assaults.

sentences.zh: 既而大軍复鎮江、瓜洲，急攻江寧，賊圖牽掣，大舉犯南陵，紹良擊走之。

translations.literal: Subsequently the great army recovered Zhenjiang and Guazhou and urgently attacked Jiangning; the rebels sought to tie down [our forces] and mounted a great offensive against Nanling — Shaoliang struck and drove them away.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army recaptured Zhenjiang and Guazhou and pressed the assault on Jiangning, the rebels attempted to divert imperial forces with a major thrust against Nanling; Shaoliang repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 八年，進屯灣沚。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he advanced and encamped at Wanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he advanced and established camp at Wanzhi.

sentences.zh: 賊合捻匪踞黃池，紹良回援，出賊不意，大破其眾，复黃池。

translations.literal: The rebels combined with Nian bandits and occupied Huangchi; Shaoliang returned to the relief, caught the rebels unawares, greatly defeated their forces, and recovered Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels allied with Nian bandits seized Huangchi; Shaoliang rushed back, surprised them, routed their army, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 會浙江軍事日棘，分兵赴援。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang military affairs grew daily more urgent, he divided his troops to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: As the military situation in Zhejiang deteriorated daily, he dispatched a detachment to assist.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊乘虛悉馬步數万鵕而涉水，斷黃池山後接應，突攻灣沚營壘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the rebels seized the vacancy; all their cavalry and infantry, numbering tens of thousands, crossed the water with fierce speed, cut off rear support at Mount Huangchi, and suddenly attacked the Wanzhi camp fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, exploiting his weakened position, the rebels sent tens of thousands of cavalry and foot soldiers splashing through the shallows, severed his line of supply behind Mount Huangchi, and launched a surprise assault on the Wanzhi encampment.

sentences.zh: 總兵戴文英由江寧來援，戰歿，遂合圍。

translations.literal: Commander Dai Wenying came from Jiangning to the relief and died in battle; thereafter [the rebels] completed the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Dai Wenying marched from Jiangning to relieve the siege but was killed in action, after which the rebels closed their encirclement completely.

sentences.zh: 軍中餉絀食盡，紹良舉火自燔其營，率親兵血戰，死之。

translations.literal: Within the army rations were exhausted and food was gone; Shaoliang set fire and burned his own camp, led his personal guard in a bloody battle, and died.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies exhausted and provisions gone, Shaoliang set his own camp ablaze, led his bodyguard into a desperate fight, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔念紹良桂林、長沙保城前功，轉戰徽、寧之間，凡歷五載，力竭捐軀，深致憫惜。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict recalled Shaoliang's prior merit in defending Guilin and Changsha cities, his campaigning between Huizhou and Ningguo for five years in all, his strength exhausted in giving his life — deep pity was expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon report of his death, the throne recalled Shaoliang's earlier deeds in the defense of Guilin and Changsha, his five years of campaigning between Huizhou and Ningguo, and his ultimate sacrifice — and expressed profound sorrow.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and granted the posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 於殉難地方建專祠，並賜其父白金四百兩，子亨先候錄用。

translations.literal: A dedicated shrine was built at the place where he died for the state; his father was also granted four hundred taels of white silver, and his son Hengxian was recorded for future appointment.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial shrine was erected where he met his death; his father received four hundred taels of silver, and his son Hengxian was entered on the roster for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋以遺骸不得，文宗尤憫之，賜亨先員外郎銜。

translations.literal: Soon because his remains could not be recovered, Emperor Wenzong especially pitied him and granted Hengxian the brevet rank of Vice Director in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When his body could not be recovered, Emperor Wenzong showed special compassion and conferred on Hengxian the honorary rank of Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 後湖南巡撫駱秉章疏請附祀表忠祠，允之。

translations.literal: Later Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang memorialized requesting that he be added to the worship at the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang petitioned that he be enshrined alongside others in the Hall of Loyalty; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 石玉龍，湖南鳳凰廳人。

translations.literal: Shi Yulong, a native of Fenghuang Department in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yulong was a native of Fenghuang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以練勇從征，隸向​​榮、鄧紹良軍，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: He joined the campaign as a militiaman, was attached to Xiang Rong's and Deng Shaoliang's armies, and through accumulated merit rose to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a militiaman under Xiang Rong and Deng Shaoliang, rising through merit to the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，總兵秦如虎駐防涇縣，以憂去，代者難其人，紹良薦玉龍，以游擊充統將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, Commander Qin Ruhu garrisoned Jing County; he departed due to mourning, and a replacement was hard to find — Shaoliang recommended Yulong to serve as colonel acting as commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, when Commander Qin Ruhu, garrisoned at Jing County, resigned to mourn a parent and no suitable successor could be found, Shaoliang recommended Yulong to command the force in the capacity of colonel.

sentences.zh: 玉龍感奮，遇戰益力。

translations.literal: Yulong was moved and inspired; encountering battle he exerted himself all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved and energized, Yulong fought with redoubled fervor in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 從紹良复灣沚、黃池，又破賊萬級嶺，累擢副將。

translations.literal: Following Shaoliang he recovered Wanzhi and Huangchi, again defeated rebels at Wanji Ridge, and was repeatedly promoted to vice general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaoliang he helped retake Wanzhi and Huangchi and defeated the rebels at Wanji Ridge, earning successive promotions to vice general.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，賊大舉犯涇縣，迎擊於藍山嶺，初勝，賊至益眾，圍之數重，身被十餘創而殞，贈總兵加提督銜，諡剛介。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year, rebels mounted a great offensive against Jing County; he met and struck them at Lanshan Ridge. At first he was victorious, but as more rebels arrived he was surrounded in several rings; he received more than ten wounds and perished. He was posthumously granted commander with the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief, and given the posthumous title Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year, when rebels launched a major assault on Jing County, he intercepted them at Lanshan Ridge. Though he won the first clash, enemy numbers swelled until he was encircled layer upon layer; he sustained more than ten wounds and fell. He was posthumously promoted to regional commander with the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief and honored with the posthumous title Steadfast and Upright.

sentences.zh: 週天受，字百祿，四川巴縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianshou, style Bailu, a native of Ba County in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tianshou, courtesy name Bailu, was a native of Ba County in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從向榮勦賊廣西，轉戰湖南、湖北、江南，積功至游擊，賜號沙拉嗎依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, he followed Xiang Rong in suppressing rebels in Guangxi, campaigned in Hunan, Hubei, and Jiangnan, and through accumulated merit rose to colonel, being granted the title Shalamayibaturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng years he served under Xiang Rong against the rebels in Guangxi, then fought across Hunan, Hubei, and Jiangnan, rising through merit to colonel and receiving the honorific title Shalamayibaturu.

sentences.zh: 五年，皖南軍事亟，前江西巡撫張芾治徽、寧兩郡防務，乞援於向榮，乃令天受率川兵赴援，偕諸軍克婺源、休寧、石埭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, southern Anhui military affairs were urgent; former Jiangxi Governor Zhang Fei managed the defenses of the Huizhou and Ningguo prefectures and begged Xiang Rong for relief — whereupon Tianshou was ordered to lead Sichuan troops to the relief, and together with the various armies took Wuyuan, Xiuning, and Shidi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as the crisis in southern Anhui deepened, former Jiangxi Governor Zhang Fei, charged with the defenses of Huizhou and Ningguo, appealed to Xiang Rong for aid. Tianshou was sent with Sichuan troops and, joining the imperial forces, captured Wuyuan, Xiuning, and Shidi.

sentences.zh: 六年，援太平，連破賊於花橋、西溪，進規涇縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he went to relieve Taiping, continuously defeated rebels at Huaqiao and Xixi, and advanced to plan the recovery of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched to relieve Taiping, won successive victories at Huaqiao and Xixi, and pressed toward the recovery of Jing County.

sentences.zh: 大敗賊於雙坑寺，復其城，擢副將。

translations.literal: He greatly defeated the rebels at Shuangkeng Temple and recovered its city; he was promoted to vice general.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels at Shuangkeng Temple and retook the city, earning promotion to vice general.

sentences.zh: 會休寧復為賊踞，官軍戰不利，張芾檄天受助剿，連捷。

translations.literal: When Xiuning was again occupied by rebels and the government army's battle was not favorable, Zhang Fei ordered Tianshou to assist in the suppression; he won in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuning fell again to the rebels and imperial forces faltered, Zhang Fei dispatched Tianshou to assist; he won a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 進毀石嶺、萬安街賊壘，會攻休寧，再复之，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He advanced to destroy the rebel forts at Shiling and Wan'an Street, joined in the attack on Xiuning, and again recovered it; he was recorded for appointment as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the rebel strongholds at Shiling and Wan'an Street, joined the assault on Xiuning, and retook the city, being marked for appointment as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，再复婺源，授福建漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he again recovered Wuyuan and was appointed regional commander of Zhangzhou Garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he recaptured Wuyuan and was appointed regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 賊踞陵陽鎮，值中秋令節，夜半出不意縱火攻之，盡毀賊營。

translations.literal: The rebels occupied Lingyang Town; on the Mid-Autumn festival night he unexpectedly set fire and attacked them, completely destroying the rebel camps.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels held Lingyang Town, he struck on the Mid-Autumn night with a surprise fire attack that burned their camps to the ground.

sentences.zh: 复破賊於祁門五里牌，搗其巢，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Wulipai in Qimen, raided their nest, and captured and beheaded very many.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed the rebels at Wulipai in Qimen, stormed their base, and killed or captured a great number.

sentences.zh: 八年，援浙江，將軍福興令守衢州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he went to relieve Zhejiang; General Fuxing ordered him to defend Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent to relieve Zhejiang; General Fuxing assigned him to hold Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 天受以浙西完善地，不可為賊擾，主扼樟樹潭。

translations.literal: Tianshou held that western Zhejiang was intact territory and must not be disturbed by rebels; he advocated holding Zhangshutan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou argued that western Zhejiang, still intact, must not be yielded to the rebels, and insisted on holding Zhangshutan.

sentences.zh: 賊竄龍遊，天受留軍守壘，自率千人趨湯溪、宣平，賊引去。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Longyou; Tianshou left troops to guard the fort and personally led a thousand men to hurry to Tangxi and Xuanping; the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels slipped toward Longyou, Tianshou left a garrison in place and personally led a thousand men in a rapid march on Tangxi and Xuanping, forcing the enemy to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 和春疏言天受知兵，能佔先著，而力單，遣其弟天培往助之，詔加提督銜，督辦浙江防剿事宜。

translations.literal: He Chun memorialized that Tianshou understood warfare and could seize the initiative, yet his strength was insufficient; he sent Tianshou's younger brother Tianpei to assist him. An edict added the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief and charged him with supervising Zhejiang defense and suppression affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun reported that Tianshou was a capable commander who could seize the initiative but lacked sufficient force, and sent his younger brother Tianpei to assist. The throne conferred on him the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief and placed him in charge of Zhejiang's defense and pacification.

sentences.zh: 天受嚴守金華，令天培复武義，又會江南軍复永康。

translations.literal: Tianshou strictly defended Jinhua, ordered Tianpei to recover Wuyi, and again joined Jiangnan forces in recovering Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou held Jinhua firmly, sent Tianpei to retake Wuyi, and joined Jiangnan forces in recovering Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 張芾劾其驕縱，縱兵搶掠，詔罷總統，仍責勦賊。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei impeached him for arrogance and lax discipline and for allowing his troops to plunder; an edict removed him as supreme commander but still charged him with suppressing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei impeached him for arrogance, indiscipline, and condoning looting by his troops; the throne stripped him of supreme command but still held him responsible for suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 天受方連克縉雲、宣平、溫州，於是浙江巡撫晏端書疏陳援浙功，為白被劾之枉。

translations.literal: Tianshou was then continuously taking Jinyun, Xuanping, and Wenzhou; thereupon Zhejiang Governor Yan Duanshu memorialized setting forth his merits in relieving Zhejiang and vindicating the injustice of the impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou was then winning a succession of victories at Jinyun, Xuanping, and Wenzhou; Zhejiang Governor Yan Duanshu memorialized in his defense, detailing his service in Zhejiang and refuting the charges against him.

sentences.zh: 詔以浙事漸平，命偕弟天培及總兵饒廷選等進援福建，連戰皆捷，复浦城，而賊回竄江西，复犯皖南。

translations.literal: An edict, because Zhejiang affairs were gradually pacified, ordered him together with his brother Tianpei and Commander Rao Tingxuan and others to advance in relief of Fujian; successive battles were all victorious and Pucheng was recovered, but the rebels fled back into Jiangxi and again invaded southern Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang grew more secure, the throne ordered him, together with Tianpei, Commander Rao Tingxuan, and others, to advance into Fujian. They won every engagement and retook Pucheng, but the rebels doubled back into Jiangxi and again threatened southern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 命署湖南提督，回軍防徽州，節制諸軍，從張芾之請也。

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as Hunan provincial commander-in-chief, return his army to defend Huizhou, and command the various armies — at Zhang Fei's request.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhang Fei's request, he was appointed acting provincial commander-in-chief of Hunan, recalled to defend Huizhou, and placed in command of the regional forces.

sentences.zh: 九年，進軍寧國，賊犯石埭、太平、涇縣，皆遣將擊走之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he advanced his army to Ningguo; when rebels invaded Shidi, Taiping, and Jing County, he dispatched generals to strike and drive them away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he marched on Ningguo; whenever rebels threatened Shidi, Taiping, or Jing County, he sent subordinates to repulse them.

sentences.zh: 十年春，官軍連捷於涇縣、旌德，賊復入浙境，坐防剿不力，褫勇號，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, the government army won continuously at Jing County and Jingde; the rebels again entered Zhejiang territory. For ineffective defense and suppression, his brave title was stripped and he was dismissed from office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year, imperial forces won repeated victories at Jing County and Jingde, yet the rebels again crossed into Zhejiang. For failing to contain them, he was stripped of his honorific title and dismissed from office, though kept on duty.

sentences.zh: 時江南大營再潰，軍事愈棘。

translations.literal: At that time the great Jiangnan camp collapsed again, and military affairs grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: By then the main Jiangnan army had collapsed once more, and the military situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 張芾疏言：「寧防將弁大半籍隸湖南，皆鄧紹良舊部，習氣甚深。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei memorialized: "Most of the Ningguo defense officers and men are by registry attached to Hunan — all old subordinates of Deng Shaoliang — and their habits run very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei wrote: "Most of the officers and men defending Ningguo are Hunan men on the rolls, veterans of Deng Shaoliang's command, and deeply set in their old ways.

sentences.zh: 天受雖力求整頓，轉滋疑謗，請歸曾國籓節制。」

translations.literal: Though Tianshou strove to rectify matters, this only bred suspicion and slander; I request that they be placed under Zeng Guofan's command."
translations.idiomatic: Though Tianshou has tried hard to impose discipline, his efforts have only bred suspicion and resentment. I ask that these troops be placed under Zeng Guofan's command."

sentences.zh: 國籓亦言其兵不可用，別調募新軍，倉猝不能至。

translations.literal: Guofan also said his troops were unusable and separately ordered the recruitment of a new army, which in haste could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan likewise declared the troops unfit for service and ordered new forces raised, but they could not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 天受偕江長貴再复涇縣，而賊糾大股犯寧國，勢甚張，天受激勵飢軍力禦。

translations.literal: Tianshou together with Jiang Changgui again recovered Jing County, but the rebels gathered a large force and invaded Ningguo; their momentum was very strong. Tianshou roused his hungry army and exerted strength to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou and Jiang Changgui retook Jing County, but the rebels mustered a large force against Ningguo with overwhelming momentum; Tianshou rallied his starving troops and threw them into the defense.

sentences.zh: 既而徽州陷，餉道梗絕，遣去城中居民萬餘，誓以身殉。

translations.literal: Subsequently Huizhou fell; the supply route was cut off. More than ten thousand city residents were sent away, and he swore to die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizhou fell and supply lines were severed, he evacuated more than ten thousand civilians from the city and vowed to die defending it.

sentences.zh: 八月，兵敗於廟埠。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the army was defeated at Miaobu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his forces were defeated at Miaobu.

sentences.zh: 天受督隊守北門，大雨，火器不燃，城陷，巷戰死之。

translations.literal: Tianshou supervised his unit in defending the north gate. In heavy rain the firearms would not ignite; the city fell, and he died fighting in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou held the north gate under his direct command. A downpour dampened the gunpowder; the city fell, and he died fighting in the streets.

sentences.zh: 詔复天受原官，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠壯；

translations.literal: An edict restored Tianshou's original office, granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang;
translations.idiomatic: The throne restored his former rank, awarded the combined hereditary titles of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored him with the posthumous name Loyal and Stalwart;

sentences.zh: 以其弟天培、天孚先皆殉節，命於四川省城及本縣合建專祠。

translations.literal: Because his younger brothers Tianpei and Tianfu had both earlier died for the state, an order was issued to build a dedicated shrine jointly in the Sichuan provincial capital and in his home county.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brothers Tianpei and Tianfu had already died in the service of the dynasty, the court ordered a joint memorial shrine erected in the Sichuan provincial capital and in their home county.

sentences.zh: 天培，由行伍從征廣西，累擢守備，隸向榮軍。

translations.literal: Tianpei, from the ranks followed the campaign in Guangxi, was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander, and was attached to Xiang Rong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei rose from the ranks, campaigning in Guangxi under Xiang Rong, and was promoted through successive grades to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，從破高資蔡家窯及壩西賊壘，賜號衛勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, he followed in the capture of the rebel forts at Gaozi Caijiayao and Baxi, and was granted the title Weiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he took part in storming the rebel positions at Gaozi, Caijiayao, and Baxi, and received the honorific title Weiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 七年，克東壩，平寶堰賊巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he took Dongba and pacified the rebel nest at Baoyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he captured Dongba and destroyed the rebel base at Baoyan.

sentences.zh: 連戰於鄔山、尖山，克溧水，又破賊於鎮江虎頭山，累擢貴州定廣協副將。

translations.literal: He fought continuously at Wushan and Jianshan, took Lishui, again defeated rebels at Hutou Mountain in Zhenjiang, and was repeatedly promoted to vice commander of Dingguang in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After successive battles at Wushan and Jianshan he took Lishui and defeated the rebels at Hutou Mountain near Zhenjiang, earning repeated promotions to vice commander of the Dingguang Brigade in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 克瓜洲，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He took Guazhou and was recorded for appointment as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Guazhou and was marked for appointment as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，授雲南鶴麗鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed regional commander of Heli Garrison in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed regional commander of the Heli garrison in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 先後偕張國樑破賊秣陵關及江寧南門外，功皆最。

translations.literal: Successively together with Zhang Guoliang he defeated rebels at Miling Pass and outside the south gate of Jiangning; in merit he ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He fought alongside Zhang Guoliang to defeat the rebels at Miling Pass and outside Jiangning's south gate, distinguishing himself above the other generals.

sentences.zh: 和春知其善戰，令赴浙江援其兄天受，迭克武義、龍泉，追賊入閩，克浦城。

translations.literal: He Chun knew he was skilled in battle and ordered him to go to Zhejiang to relieve his elder brother Tianshou; he successively took Wuyi and Longquan, pursued the rebels into Fujian, and took Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing his prowess, He Chun sent him to Zhejiang to aid his brother Tianshou. He captured Wuyi and Longquan in succession, pursued the rebels into Fujian, and took Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 會江南、北軍事急，天培回援。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan and northern military affairs grew urgent, Tianpei returned to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When crises erupted in Jiangnan and the north, Tianpei hurried back to assist.

sentences.zh: 九年春，賊分六路攻浦口，張國樑督諸軍禦戰，天培首先躍馬衝陣，各軍乘之，殲賊無算。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, rebels divided into six routes to attack Pukou; Zhang Guoliang supervised the various armies in resisting battle. Tianpei was the first to leap on his horse and charge the formation; the various armies followed, annihilating countless rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year the rebels attacked Pukou along six routes. Zhang Guoliang directed the defense; Tianpei was first to spur his horse into the enemy lines, and the other units followed, slaughtering the rebels without number.

sentences.zh: 賊築壘於雙陽、蕭家圩，別由九洑洲出悍眾來撲，天培分兵擊之，三戰三捷，功出諸將上，擢湖北提督，遂駐防浦口。

translations.literal: The rebels built forts at Shuangyang and Xiaojiawei; separately a fierce force came out from Jiufuzhou to assault. Tianpei divided his troops to strike them; three battles, three victories — his merit ranked above the various generals. He was promoted to Hubei provincial commander-in-chief and then garrisoned Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fortified Shuangyang and Xiaojiawei and sent a fierce column from Jiufuzhou to attack, Tianpei divided his force and met them in three successive victories, outperforming every other commander. He was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Hubei and stationed at Pukou.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，匪首陳玉成糾眾十餘萬犯江浦，天培乘其初至，痛殲之。

translations.literal: That winter, the bandit chief Chen Yucheng gathered a force of more than one hundred thousand and invaded Jiangpu; Tianpei, while they had just arrived, fiercely annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebel leader Chen Yucheng mustered more than a hundred thousand men against Jiangpu; Tianpei struck as they were still arriving and inflicted a devastating defeat.

sentences.zh: 既而賊麕集，後路為所抄襲，裹創血戰，力竭陣亡。

translations.literal: Subsequently the rebels gathered in crowds; his rear route was cut off in a raid. Wounded, he fought a bloody battle, his strength exhausted, and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels massed and cut off his retreat, he fought on despite his wounds until his strength gave out and he fell on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 優詔賜卹，贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡武壯。

translations.literal: A special edict granted condolence payments; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and granted the posthumous title Wuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued a special edict of condolence, posthumously ennobled him as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored him with the posthumous name Martial and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 天孚，從兄天受軍轉戰，以功洊保參將，留江蘇補用。

translations.literal: Tianfu followed his elder brother Tianshou's army in campaigning, and through merit was repeatedly promoted to regimental commander; he remained in Jiangsu awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu served in his elder brother Tianshou's command, rising through merit to regimental commander, and remained in Jiangsu awaiting formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，賊犯皖南，副將石玉龍戰死涇縣南山嶺。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng, rebels invaded southern Anhui; Vice General Shi Yulong died in battle at Nanshan Ridge in Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianfeng, when rebels invaded southern Anhui, Vice General Shi Yulong was killed at Nanshan Ridge in Jing County.

sentences.zh: 天孚屯灣沚，馳百里往援，要擊於章家渡，大破之，由是以驍勇名。

translations.literal: Tianfu was encamped at Wanzhi; he galloped a hundred li to go to the relief and intercepted at Zhangjiadu, greatly defeating them; from this he became known for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu, encamped at Wanzhi, rode a hundred li to the rescue, intercepted the enemy at Zhangjiadu, and routed them — earning a reputation for fearless valor.

sentences.zh: 尋援金壇，會諸軍連戰解其圍。

translations.literal: Soon he went to relieve Jintan; joining the various armies he fought continuously and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to relieve Jintan and, joining allied forces in continuous fighting, broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 十年，江南大營潰，閏三月，賊首李世賢大舉复圍金壇。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the great Jiangnan camp collapsed; in the intercalary third month the bandit chief Li Shixian mounted a great offensive and again besieged Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, after the collapse of the main Jiangnan army, the rebel leader Li Shixian launched a major offensive and once again encircled Jintan in the intercalary third month.

sentences.zh: 天孚偕總兵蕭知音、參將艾得勝、知縣李淮同守之。

translations.literal: Tianfu together with Commander Xiao Zhiyin, Regimental Commander Ai Desheng, and Magistrate Li Huai jointly defended it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu defended the city alongside Commander Xiao Zhiyin, Regimental Commander Ai Desheng, and Magistrate Li Huai.

sentences.zh: 淮素得人心，兵民合力，屢卻賊。

translations.literal: Li Huai had long won the people's hearts; soldiers and civilians joined strength and repeatedly repulsed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai enjoyed the people's trust, and soldiers and civilians fought together to repulse repeated assaults.

sentences.zh: 時江南軍事大壞，孤城援絕。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangnan military affairs were greatly ruined; the isolated city was cut off from relief.
translations.idiomatic: By then the military situation in Jiangnan had collapsed entirely, and the isolated city was beyond reach of any relief force.

sentences.zh: 天孚馳書兄天受，始疏聞，屢詔促鎮江副都統巴棟阿偕總兵馮子材赴援，卒不至。

translations.literal: Tianfu sent a dispatch to his elder brother Tianshou; only then was it first reported to the throne. Repeated edicts urgently ordered Vice Commander of the Garrison Badong'a of Zhenjiang together with Commander Feng Zicai to go to the relief, but in the end they did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu wrote urgently to his brother Tianshou, and only then did word reach the court. Repeated imperial orders summoned Badong'a, vice commander of the Zhenjiang garrison, and Commander Feng Zicai to the rescue, but they never came.

sentences.zh: 凡守百四十餘日，糧盡，軍無固志。

translations.literal: In all they defended for more than one hundred forty days; grain was exhausted and the army had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred and forty days of siege, provisions ran out and the garrison's resolve began to fail.

sentences.zh: 知音等原率兵民突圍走鎮江，淮不可，誓死守，乃中止。

translations.literal: Zhiyin and the others originally led soldiers and civilians in a breakout toward Zhenjiang; Li Huai would not agree and swore to defend to the death, and so they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhiyin and others proposed breaking out with soldiers and civilians toward Zhenjiang, but Li Huai refused and vowed to hold to the death, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 屢獲賊內應，斬之。

translations.literal: They repeatedly captured rebel collaborators within [the city] and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly uncovered rebel collaborators inside the walls and executed them.

sentences.zh: 城陷先一日，偵知將有變，竟夜登陴，至旦，分半隊休息，值大霧，叛兵遽起，先戕天孚。

translations.literal: One day before the city fell, through reconnaissance they learned that a change was imminent; all night they mounted the battlements, and at dawn they divided half the unit to rest. A great fog arose; mutinous soldiers suddenly rose and first killed Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the city's fall, scouts detected that treachery was afoot. The defenders manned the walls all night; at dawn half the garrison was sent to rest. A thick fog rolled in, mutinous troops rose suddenly, and Tianfu was the first to be cut down.

sentences.zh: 賊乃梯登，知音、得勝突圍出，淮死之。

translations.literal: The rebels then scaled [the walls] with ladders; Zhiyin and Desheng broke out of the encirclement and got out; Li Huai died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then scaled the walls. Xiao Zhiyin and Ai Desheng fought their way out, while Li Huai died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈天孚總兵，予騎都尉世職，諡威毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Tianfu was posthumously granted regional commander, given the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and granted the posthumous title Weiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Upon report of his death, Tianfu was posthumously promoted to regional commander, awarded the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant, and honored with the posthumous name Formidable and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 饒廷選，字枚臣，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Rao Tingxuan, style Meichen, a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Rao Tingxuan, courtesy name Meichen, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 以行伍洊升千總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was repeatedly promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks through repeated promotions to company commander.

sentences.zh: 道光中，從剿台灣有功，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang era, he followed the suppression of Taiwan with merit and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he served in the Taiwan campaign with distinction and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從水師提督竇振彪出洋擒海盜，擢漳州營都司。

translations.literal: He followed Naval Commander Dou Zhenbiao out to sea to capture pirates and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhangzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Naval Commander Dou Zhenbiao, he captured pirates at sea and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷游擊，治匪無株連，得民心。

translations.literal: He was transferred to colonel; in governing bandits he did not implicate the innocent by association and won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to colonel, he suppressed banditry without punishing the innocent by association and won popular trust.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，奉檄赴詔安治械鬥，而潮州會匪襲漳州，伏兵於城中突起，鎮道皆遇害。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, he received orders to go to Zhao'an to suppress armed feuding, but Chaozhou secret-society bandits raided Zhangzhou; ambush troops suddenly rose within the city and the garrison commander and circuit intendant were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was dispatched to Zhao'an to quell armed feuds, but Chaozhou secret-society rebels struck Zhangzhou; hidden troops rose inside the city and both the garrison commander and the circuit intendant were slain.

sentences.zh: 廷選聞變，間道馳還，號召鄉民千餘，城民應之。

translations.literal: Tingxuan heard of the disturbance, took a bypath and galloped back, and summoned more than a thousand local militiamen; the city people responded.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the uprising, Tingxuan took a back route and rode hard to the city, rallying more than a thousand local militiamen to whom the townspeople rallied in turn.

sentences.zh: 賊遁，旋復大至。

translations.literal: The rebels fled; soon they again came in great force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew, but soon returned in strength.

sentences.zh: 廷選率鄉團固守，迭戰破賊，擒賊首謝厚等，遂署漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Tingxuan led the local militia in firm defense, repeatedly defeated the rebels in battle, captured the bandit chiefs Xie Hou and others, and was then appointed acting regional commander of Zhangzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan led the local militia in a stout defense, won repeated victories, captured rebel leaders including Xie Hou, and was appointed acting regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 外剿內撫，期年始平。

translations.literal: Externally he suppressed, internally he pacified; after a full year it was at last pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning without and pacifying within, he restored order after a full year.

sentences.zh: 總督王懿德薦其才可大用，四年，授貴州安義鎮總兵，留署福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wang Yide recommended that his talent could be greatly employed; in the fourth year he was appointed regional commander of Anyi Garrison in Guizhou and remained acting Fujian land forces provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wang Yide recommended him as a man of great capacity; in the fourth year he was appointed regional commander of the Anyi garrison in Guizhou while continuing to serve as acting provincial commander-in-chief of Fujian's land forces.

sentences.zh: 五年，粵匪陷廣信，浙江戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Guangdong rebels took Guangxin and Zhejiang went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Guangdong rebels captured Guangxin, Zhejiang was placed on high alert.

sentences.zh: 廷選赴援，扼衢州。

translations.literal: Tingxuan went to the relief and held Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan marched to the relief and held Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋楚軍克廣信，賊知浙境有備，走徽州。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the Chu army recovered Guangxin; the rebels, learning that the Zhejiang border was defended, fled toward Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thereafter the Hunan army recovered Guangxin. Learning that Zhejiang was prepared, the rebels withdrew toward Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊酋楊輔清复圖廣信以擾浙。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the rebel chieftain Yang Fuqing again schemed to take Guangxin and harass Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the rebel chieftain Yang Fuqing again plotted to seize Guangxin and raid Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 廣信兵僅數百，知府沈葆楨馳書告急。

translations.literal: Guangxin had only a few hundred troops; Prefect Shen Baozhen sent an urgent dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxin held barely a few hundred soldiers; Prefect Shen Baozhen sent an urgent plea for help.

sentences.zh: 廷選方駐甲玉山，曰：「賊得廣信，則玉山不守，而浙危矣。」

translations.literal: Tingxuan was then encamped at Yushan and said: "If the rebels take Guangxin, Yushan cannot be held and Zhejiang will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan was then encamped at Yushan and said, "If the rebels take Guangxin, Yushan cannot be held and all of Zhejiang will be in peril."

sentences.zh: 值大雨水漲，駛舟急行，抵廣信。
