translations.literal: Heavy rains had swollen the rivers; he sailed in haste and reached Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains had swollen the rivers; he put to boat at once and reached Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 賊已至城西太平橋，初諜城中無兵，及見旌旗，賊為奪氣。

translations.literal: The rebels had already reached Taiping Bridge west of the city. Their scouts at first reported no troops within; when they saw banners and flags, the rebels lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already reached Taiping Bridge west of the city. Spies had first reported the town undefended; at the sight of banners and flags the enemy lost heart.

sentences.zh: 廷選所部僅千餘人，屢出奇擊賊。

translations.literal: Tingxuan commanded barely more than a thousand men, yet repeatedly struck the rebels with surprise attacks.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan had barely a thousand men under his command, yet again and again he struck the rebels with surprise attacks.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大至，部將畢定邦、賴高翔皆勇敢，獻計曰：「今賊不知我虛實，以我能戰，後路必有大兵。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels arrived in force. His subordinate officers Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang were both brave men; they presented a plan, saying: "The rebels do not know our true strength. Because we have fought so well, they must believe a large army waits in our rear.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels came in force. His officers Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang, both men of courage, offered a plan: "The rebels do not know our true strength. Because we have fought so fiercely, they must believe a great army waits behind us.

sentences.zh: 若稍退，賊追我，且立盡。

translations.literal: If we withdraw even slightly, they will pursue us and we will be wiped out at once.
translations.idiomatic: If we fall back even a little, they will pursue us and we will be destroyed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 當速決死戰。」

translations.literal: We must quickly resolve on a fight to the death."
translations.idiomatic: We must decide at once on a battle to the death."

sentences.zh: 廷選用其言，明日開城奮擊，自晨至日暮，毀其長圍，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Tingxuan adopted their counsel. The next day he opened the gates and struck fiercely; from morning until evening he broke their long encirclement, and the army's morale soared.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan took their advice. The next day he opened the gates and struck with all his might; from dawn to dusk he broke the long encirclement, and the army's spirit rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 越二日，賊引去，賜號西林巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Two days later the rebels withdrew; he was granted the title Xilin Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the rebels withdrew, and he was granted the honorific Xilin Baturol.

sentences.zh: 閩、浙大吏與江西督防者不慊，檄廷選速回師保浙。

translations.literal: Senior officials of Fujian and Zhejiang and the Jiangxi border-defense commander were displeased and ordered Tingxuan to march back at once to defend Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials of Fujian and Zhejiang, together with the Jiangxi border-defense commander, were displeased and ordered Tingxuan to hurry back and defend Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 廷選待接防兵至始行，廣信民感其義。

translations.literal: Tingxuan waited until relief troops arrived before departing; the people of Guangxin were moved by his sense of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxuan waited until relief troops arrived before he marched away, and the people of Guangxin were deeply moved by his devotion.

sentences.zh: 七年，調衢州鎮總兵，會皖軍克婺源。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to regional commander of the Quzhou garrison; about that time the Anhui army took Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made regional commander of the Quzhou garrison; about then the Anhui army recovered Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊首石達開大舉犯浙，廷選分軍援廣豐，自守衢州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the rebel leader Shi Dakai invaded Zhejiang in force. Tingxuan detached troops to relieve Guangfeng while he himself held Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the rebel leader Shi Dakai invaded Zhejiang in force. Tingxuan sent part of his army to relieve Guangfeng while he himself held Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊驟至，穴地攻城，城圮者三，皆擊卻之，守七十餘日。

translations.literal: The rebels came suddenly, mined beneath the walls, and three times brought sections of wall down; each time he beat them back and held for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came suddenly, tunneled beneath the walls, and three times brought sections of the ramparts down; each time he drove them back and held the city for more than seventy days.

sentences.zh: 巡撫晏端書劾其久未解圍，又失江山、常山、開化三縣，奪職。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Yan Duanshu impeached him for failing to lift the siege for so long and for losing the three counties of Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua; his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Yan Duanshu impeached him for leaving the siege unresolved so long and for losing Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua; he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，圍解，三縣皆复，授南贛鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Before long the siege was lifted and all three counties were recovered; he was appointed regional commander of the Nangan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the siege lifted, all three counties were restored, and he received appointment as regional commander of the Nangan garrison.

sentences.zh: 王懿德檄召回援閩境，以病未行，遽劾，革職留營。

translations.literal: Wang Yide ordered him recalled to relieve Fujian, but illness kept him from going; he was suddenly impeached, removed from office, and kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yide ordered him recalled to relieve Fujian, but illness kept him from marching; he was suddenly impeached, stripped of rank, and kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 八年，會克連城、龍巖，仍補南贛鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Liancheng and Longyan were taken, he was restored to the Nangan garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Liancheng and Longyan were recovered, he was restored to command of the Nangan garrison.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓奏以代沈葆楨守廣信，從民望也。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan memorialized that he should replace Shen Baozhen in holding Guangxin — yielding to popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan memorialized that he should replace Shen Baozhen in holding Guangxin, yielding to the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵匪复犯浙，廷選赴援，复淳安，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Guangdong rebels again invaded Zhejiang. Tingxuan marched to the relief, recovered Chun'an, and was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Guangdong rebels again invaded Zhejiang, Tingxuan hurried to their aid, retook Chun'an, and was raised to provincial commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，攻克嚴州，進規浦江，賊大至，不敵，退保諸暨，而杭州被圍急。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year he took Yanzhou and advanced toward Pujiang; the rebels came in force, he could not match them, and fell back to defend Zhuji while Hangzhou was closely besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eleventh year he took Yanzhou and advanced on Pujiang; the rebels came in overwhelming force, he could not stand against them, and fell back to Zhuji even as Hangzhou was pressed hard by siege.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王有齡促回援，廷選舊部僅漳勇數百、楚軍二千。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Wang Youlin pressed him to return to the relief; of Tingxuan's old command only a few hundred Zhangzhou militia and two thousand Chu troops remained.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Wang Youlin urged him to hurry back to the relief; of Tingxuan's old command only a few hundred Zhangzhou militiamen and two thousand Hunan troops remained.

sentences.zh: 事急，收集江南潰卒，皆不任戰，徒激忠義，勉以當賊。

translations.literal: The crisis was acute. He gathered routed troops from Jiangnan, none fit for battle; he could only stir their loyalty and urge them to stand against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis was acute. He gathered routed soldiers from Jiangnan, none fit to fight; he could only rouse their loyalty and urge them to face the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊於城外海潮寺、鳳凰山為堅壁，隔絕內外。

translations.literal: The rebels built strong fortifications at Haichao Temple and Fenghuang Mountain outside the walls, cutting off communication between within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified Haichao Temple and Fenghuang Mountain outside the walls, severing the city from the outside world.

sentences.zh: 困守七十餘日，糧盡，士卒飢餓。

translations.literal: Besieged for more than seventy days, provisions ran out and the soldiers starved.
translations.idiomatic: After more than seventy days under siege, grain was exhausted and the soldiers went hungry.

sentences.zh: 十一月，城陷，巷戰死之，贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡果壯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the city fell; he died fighting in the streets. He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous title Guozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the city fell; he died fighting in the streets. He was posthumously ennobled as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored with the posthumous title Resolute and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 入祀昭忠祠，於杭州建專祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was entered in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, and a dedicated shrine was raised for him at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄廷傑，弟廷夔，同戰死，附祀焉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tingjie and younger brother Tingkui died fighting alongside him and were enshrined there as well.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tingjie and younger brother Tingkui fell in the same battle and were enshrined beside him.

sentences.zh: 既而曾國籓、沈葆楨以廷選守廣信功，奏請建祠廣信，以副將畢定邦、賴高翔附祀。

translations.literal: Later Zeng Guofan and Shen Baozhen, citing Tingxuan's merit in holding Guangxin, memorialized for a shrine at Guangxin with the brigade commanders Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang enshrined beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zeng Guofan and Shen Baozhen, citing Tingxuan's merit in holding Guangxin, memorialized for a shrine at Guangxin with the brigade commanders Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang enshrined with him.

sentences.zh: 文瑞，克什克特恩氏，蒙古鑲藍旗人，荊州駐防。

translations.literal: Wenrui, of the Keshiketen clan, was a Mongol of the Bordered Blue Banner, stationed at the Jingzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrui, of the Keshiketen clan, was a Mongol bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner, garrisoned at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 由驍騎校從軍，轉戰湖北、安徽，累擢江西撫標中軍參將。

translations.literal: Starting as a vanguard cavalry officer, he campaigned in Hubei and Anhui and rose in time to deputy brigade commander of the Jiangxi provincial garrison's central battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a vanguard cavalry officer, he fought in Hubei and Anhui and eventually became deputy brigade commander of the Jiangxi provincial garrison's central battalion.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，赴援浙江，克餘杭，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he went to relieve Zhejiang, took Yuhang, and was registered at regional commander rank for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he marched to relieve Zhejiang, took Yuhang, and was entered on the rolls at regional commander rank.

sentences.zh: 解湖州圍，賜號唐木濟特依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He lifted the siege of Huzhou and was granted the title Tangmujiteyi Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege of Huzhou and was granted the honorific Tangmujiteyi Baturol.

sentences.zh: 授處州鎮總兵，進剿金華。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of the Chuzhou garrison and advanced to suppress the rebels at Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regional commander of the Chuzhou garrison and advanced to drive the rebels from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 賊圍浦江，文瑞嬰城固守，屢出奇破賊營，踰月乃陷，詔免其處分。

translations.literal: When the rebels besieged Pujiang, Wenrui held the city in a desperate defense, repeatedly broke rebel camps with surprise attacks, and only after more than a month did the city fall; an edict exempted him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged Pujiang, Wenrui held the city in desperate defense, again and again breaking rebel camps with surprise attacks; only after more than a month did the city fall, and an edict spared him punishment.

sentences.zh: 回援杭州，入城助守，城陷死之，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡果毅。

translations.literal: He returned to relieve Hangzhou, entered the city to help defend it, and died when the city fell. He was granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant and given the posthumous title Guoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to relieve Hangzhou, entered the city to help defend it, and died when the city fell. He was granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant and honored with the posthumous title Resolute and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 彭斯舉，湖南平江人。

translations.literal: Peng Siju was a native of Pingjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siju came from Pingjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以團練勦賊，從李元度為平江軍營官。

translations.literal: He raised local militia to suppress bandits and served under Li Yuandu as an officer of the Pingjiang army camp.
translations.idiomatic: He organized local militia against bandits and served under Li Yuandu as an officer in the Pingjiang army camp.

sentences.zh: 戰湖口、東鄉、貴溪、安仁、玉山，積功晉秩知府。

translations.literal: He fought at Hukou, Dongxiang, Guixi, Anren, and Yushan; with accumulated merit he was promoted to the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Hukou, Dongxiang, Guixi, Anren, and Yushan; with accumulated merit he rose to the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 元度罷去，留所部五營隸斯舉，始獨將一軍。

translations.literal: When Yuandu was dismissed, his five battalions were left under Siju's command, and for the first time he led an army on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuandu was removed, his five battalions were placed under Siju's command, and for the first time he led an army alone.

sentences.zh: 會攻景德鎮，饒廷選見而器之，調援浙江，破賊於淳安，復其城，擢道員，留浙補用。

translations.literal: During the attack on Jingdezhen, Rao Tingxuan took notice of him and valued his ability; he was transferred to relieve Zhejiang, defeated the rebels at Chun'an and recovered the city, was promoted to circuit intendant, and remained in Zhejiang awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the attack on Jingdezhen, Rao Tingxuan marked him out and valued his talent; he was transferred to relieve Zhejiang, broke the rebels at Chun'an and recovered the city, was promoted to circuit intendant, and remained in Zhejiang awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 駐守千秋關，賊大至，搏戰竟日，潰圍出，移防海寧。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Qianqiu Pass; when the rebels came in force he fought all day, broke out of the encirclement, and shifted his defense to Haining.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Qianqiu Pass; when the rebels came in force he fought all day, broke through the encirclement, and shifted his defense to Haining.

sentences.zh: 會攻嚴州，下之。

translations.literal: He joined the attack on Yanzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attack on Yanzhou and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進援廣信，而所部留駐常山者索餉譁潰，斯舉率親兵赴杭州，乞解軍事回籍，巡撫王有齡留管營務處。

translations.literal: Advancing to relieve Guangxin, he found troops he had left at Changshan rioting for pay and dispersing. Siju led his personal guard to Hangzhou, asked to be relieved of military duties and return home, but Provincial Governor Wang Youlin kept him to manage camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As he advanced to relieve Guangxin, troops he had left at Changshan mutinied for pay and scattered. Siju led his personal guard to Hangzhou and asked to be relieved of command and sent home, but Provincial Governor Wang Youlin kept him to manage camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 斯舉建議，省城米糧來自寧、紹，錢塘江距城三里，當築甬道，兵護之，運道乃無虞。

translations.literal: Siju proposed that since the provincial capital's grain came from Ningbo and Shaoxing, and the Qiantang River lay three li from the city, a causeway should be built under military escort so the supply route would be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Siju proposed that since the provincial capital's grain came from Ningbo and Shaoxing, and the Qiantang River lay three li from the city walls, a causeway should be built under military escort so the supply line would be safe.

sentences.zh: 未及行而賊至，城中竟以絕糧陷。

translations.literal: Before this could be carried out the rebels arrived, and the city ultimately fell for lack of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Before this could be done the rebels arrived, and the city ultimately fell for want of grain.

sentences.zh: 斯舉分守湧金門，死之。

translations.literal: Siju was assigned to defend Yongjin Gate and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Siju was posted to defend Yongjin Gate and died there.

sentences.zh: 張玉良，字璧田，四川巴縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang, courtesy name Bitian, was a native of Ba county in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang, styled Bitian, was born in Ba county, Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，由行伍從征廣西，積功至千總。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he entered service from the ranks and campaigned in Guangxi, rising with merit to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign he rose from the ranks, campaigned in Guangxi, and with accumulated merit became a company commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，從向榮至江南，戰江寧城外，屢有功，累擢永州左營游擊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Xiang Rong to Jiangnan, fought outside Jiangning, won repeated merit, and rose in time to colonel of the Yongzhou Left Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Xiang Rong to Jiangnan, fought outside Jiangning with repeated distinction, and rose in time to colonel of the Yongzhou Left Battalion.

sentences.zh: 六年，敗賊於丹陽、金壇，賜號黽勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he defeated the rebels at Danyang and Jintan and was granted the title Mianyong Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he defeated the rebels at Danyang and Jintan and was granted the honorific Mianyong Baturol.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊於溧水西門，毀其砲台，擢處州營參將。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at the west gate of Lishui, destroyed their batteries, and was promoted to deputy brigade commander of the Chuzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels again at Lishui's west gate, demolished their batteries, and was promoted to deputy brigade commander of the Chuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，克句容，加總兵銜，擢三江口協副將。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he took Jurong, was given regional commander rank, and was promoted to vice commander of the Sanjiangkou Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he captured Jurong, received regional commander rank, and was made vice commander of the Sanjiangkou Brigade.

sentences.zh: 破鎮江援賊於江濱，克鎮江，敘功以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He broke Zhenjiang relief rebels on the riverbank, took Zhenjiang, and for merit was registered at regional commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Zhenjiang relief rebels on the riverbank, took Zhenjiang, and for merit was entered on the rolls at regional commander rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，大破江寧援賊，擢甘肅巴里坤總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he inflicted a great defeat on Jiangning relief rebels and was promoted to regional commander of Barkol in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he inflicted a crushing defeat on Jiangning relief rebels and was promoted to regional commander of the Barkol garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 攻太平、金川諸門，賊眾突出，痛殲之。

translations.literal: Attacking the Taiping and Jin river gates, he met a massive rebel sortie and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: While assaulting the Taiping and Jin river gates he met a massive rebel sortie and cut them down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 馳援溧水，毀紅藍埠賊壘，克其城，斬賊千餘級，加提督銜。

translations.literal: He hurried to relieve Lishui, destroyed the rebel stockades at Honglanbu, took the city, and beheaded more than a thousand rebels; he was given provincial commander-in-chief rank.
translations.idiomatic: Racing to relieve Lishui, he destroyed the rebel stockades at Honglanbu, took the city, and beheaded more than a thousand rebels; he was then granted provincial commander-in-chief rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，會攻浦口，大捷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he joined the attack on Pukou and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he took part in the assault on Pukou and won a resounding victory.

sentences.zh: 而九洑洲之賊來援，玉良率後隊截擊，賊大潰。

translations.literal: When rebels from Jiufu Isle came to the relief, Yuliang led the rearguard in an intercepting strike and the rebels fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels from Jiufu Isle came to the relief, Yuliang led the rearguard in an intercepting strike and the rebels broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 十年春，遂乘勝克九洑洲，詔遇提督缺出題奏，尋調肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he pressed the advantage and took Jiufu Isle; an edict ordered that whenever a provincial commander-in-chief's post fell vacant he be recommended by name, and soon he was transferred to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: That spring of the tenth year he pressed his advantage and seized Jiufu Isle; an edict directed that whenever a provincial commander-in-chief's post opened he be recommended by name, and soon afterward he was transferred to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 江南大營諸將善戰者，向榮舊部多蜀將，張國樑所部多粵將。

translations.literal: Among the fighting generals of the Jiangnan Grand Camp, Xiang Rong's old command had many Sichuan officers and Zhang Guoliang's had many Guangdong officers.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jiangnan Grand Camp's best fighters, Xiang Rong's old corps counted many Sichuan officers, while Zhang Guoliang's command drew heavily on Guangdong men.

sentences.zh: 蜀將以虎坤元為首，週天培及玉良次之。

translations.literal: Among the Sichuan generals Hu Kunyuan stood first, followed by Zhou Tianpei and Yuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Sichuan generals, Hu Kunyuan ranked first, with Zhou Tianpei and Yuliang close behind.

sentences.zh: 時浙江軍事亟，議分軍赴援，咸屬望於張國樑，而圍攻江寧，功在垂成，國樑為全軍所繫，不克行。

translations.literal: At that time Zhejiang's military situation was urgent; there was talk of detaching troops for relief, and all eyes turned to Zhang Guoliang — but the siege of Jiangning was on the verge of success and the whole army depended on him; he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhejiang's military situation was urgent; detachments for relief were discussed, and all hopes rested on Zhang Guoliang — yet the siege of Jiangning was on the verge of success and the whole army depended on him, so he could not go.

sentences.zh: 坤元、天培已前歿，乃命玉良總統援浙諸軍，專辦浙江軍務，未至而杭州陷，將軍瑞昌獨堅守駐防內城，與賊相持。

translations.literal: Kunyuan and Tianpei had already died; Yuliang was then placed in overall command of the Zhejiang relief armies and charged solely with Zhejiang military affairs. Before he arrived Hangzhou fell; General Ruichang alone held firm in the garrison inner city, locked in stalemate with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan and Tianpei had already fallen; Yuliang was then placed in overall command of the armies relieving Zhejiang and charged solely with Zhejiang military affairs. Before he arrived Hangzhou fell; General Ruichang alone held firm in the garrison inner city, locked in stalemate with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 玉良率六百人馳至，出賊不意，毀武林、錢塘諸門外賊壘，梯城而上，遂復杭州。

translations.literal: Yuliang galloped up with six hundred men, caught the rebels off guard, destroyed their stockades outside the Wulin and Qiantang gates, scaled the walls by ladder, and recovered Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang raced up with six hundred men, took the rebels by surprise, tore down their stockades outside the Wulin and Qiantang gates, scaled the walls on ladders, and retook Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉為奇功，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職，擢廣西提督。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an edict praised it as an extraordinary feat; he was granted the yellow riding jacket and the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, an edict praised it as an extraordinary feat; he was granted the yellow riding jacket and the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant, and promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊之擾浙也，原以牽制江南軍，故見玉良至，則不戰遽去，由廣德分路趨江寧。

translations.literal: The rebels' raids on Zhejiang had been meant to tie down the Jiangnan army; when Yuliang arrived they withdrew without fighting and split at Guangde toward Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had raided Zhejiang to tie down the Jiangnan army; when Yuliang arrived they withdrew without fighting and split at Guangde toward Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 總督何桂清駐常州，檄玉良回援，而賊別隊已侵江南大營後路。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Guiqing was stationed at Changzhou and ordered Yuliang back to the relief, but a separate rebel column had already threatened the Jiangnan Grand Camp's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Guiqing was stationed at Changzhou and ordered Yuliang back to the relief, but a separate rebel column had already threatened the rear of the Jiangnan Grand Camp.

sentences.zh: 桂清留玉良於常州以自衛。

translations.literal: Guiqing kept Yuliang at Changzhou for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing kept Yuliang at Changzhou to guard his own person.

sentences.zh: 未幾，江寧兵潰，張國樑、和春先後殉，詔玉良代節制其軍。

translations.literal: Before long the Jiangning army collapsed; Zhang Guoliang and Hechun died in succession for the cause, and an edict put Yuliang in command of their army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jiangning army disintegrated; Zhang Guoliang and Hechun died one after another in the field, and an edict placed Yuliang in overall command of their forces.

sentences.zh: 常州陷，禦賊於無錫高橋，賊由間道出九龍山襲無錫。

translations.literal: Changzhou fell; he met the rebels at Gaogiao in Wuxi, but they took a hidden route through Jiulong Mountain and struck Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell; he met the rebels at Gaogiao in Wuxi, but they took a hidden route through Jiulong Mountain and struck Wuxi from the flank.

sentences.zh: 玉良前後受敵，退保蘇州，入城計守禦，未定，潰兵應賊，蘇州亦陷。

translations.literal: Caught between enemies front and rear, Yuliang fell back to Suzhou. He entered the city to plan a defense, but before plans were settled routed soldiers went over to the rebels and Suzhou too fell.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between enemies front and rear, Yuliang fell back to Suzhou. He entered the city to plan a defense, but before plans were settled routed soldiers went over to the rebels and Suzhou fell as well.

sentences.zh: 玉良奔杭州，褫職，隸瑞昌軍。

translations.literal: Yuliang fled to Hangzhou, was stripped of office, and was attached to Ruichang's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang fled to Hangzhou, was stripped of office, and was placed under Ruichang's command.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌令規复嚴州，繼克常山，復原官。

translations.literal: Ruichang ordered him to plan the recovery of Yanzhou; he subsequently took Changshan and was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Ruichang ordered him to plan the recovery of Yanzhou; he subsequently took Changshan and was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复遂安，而嚴州又陷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he recovered Suian, but Yanzhou fell again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he retook Suian, but Yanzhou fell once more.

sentences.zh: 玉良自江南敗衄後，兵心已渙，不能復振。

translations.literal: After his defeat in Jiangnan, Yuliang's soldiers' morale had scattered and could not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat in Jiangnan, the spirit of Yuliang's army had broken and could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 賊再攻杭州，馳援，軍不用命，自知事不可為，戰杭州城下，輒身臨前敵，力鬥，中飛砲，歿於軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked Hangzhou again he hurried to the relief, but the army would not obey; knowing the cause was lost, he fought beneath the walls of Hangzhou, always placing himself in the fore, fought fiercely, was struck by a cannonball, and died in the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Hangzhou again he hurried to the relief, but the army would not obey; knowing the cause was lost, he fought beneath the walls of Hangzhou, always placing himself in the fore, fought with all his might, was struck by a cannonball, and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，祀本籍昭忠祠，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs in his home region, and given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs in his home region, and honored with the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 魯佔鼇，四川成都人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhan'ao was a native of Chengdu in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhan'ao came from Chengdu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍官平番營守備，從向榮勦賊廣西、江南。

translations.literal: From the ranks he became garrison commander of the Pingfan camp and followed Xiang Rong to suppress bandits in Guangxi and Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to garrison commander of the Pingfan camp, he followed Xiang Rong in suppressing bandits across Guangxi and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 繼從吉爾杭阿克上海，攻鎮江，戰皆力，累擢川北鎮總兵，調建昌鎮。

translations.literal: He then followed Geleng'a to Shanghai, attacked Zhenjiang, fought with all his strength in every engagement, rose to regional commander of the North Sichuan garrison, and was transferred to the Jianchang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He next followed Geleng'a to Shanghai, fought at Zhenjiang, and threw himself into every engagement; through repeated promotion he became regional commander of the North Sichuan garrison and was transferred to the Jianchang garrison.

sentences.zh: 蘇州陷，為賊所執，罵賊被臠割，死之。

translations.literal: When Suzhou fell he was captured by the rebels; he cursed them and was cut to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou fell he was taken by the rebels; he cursed them to their faces and was hacked apart.

sentences.zh: 贈提督銜，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given provincial commander-in-chief rank and granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given provincial commander-in-chief rank and granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 劉季三，廣西武宣人。

translations.literal: Liu Jisan was a native of Wuxuan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jisan came from Wuxuan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以武舉從右江道張敬修戰桂林、全州，授左江鎮標守備。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he followed Youjiang Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingxiu in fighting at Guilin and Quanzhou and was appointed garrison commander of the Zuojiang garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: As a military licentiate he campaigned under Youjiang Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingxiu at Guilin and Quanzhou and was appointed garrison commander of the Zuojiang garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 從向榮至江南，積功至副將，賜號直勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He followed Xiang Rong to Jiangnan, rose with merit to brigade commander, and was granted the title Zhiyong Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiang Rong to Jiangnan, rose with merit to brigade commander, and was granted the honorific Zhiyong Baturol.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，大兵攻秣陵關，季三於葛塘寺設伏，出賊不意，斬關入，火之，又破六郎橋賊巢，功皆最，擢直隸通永鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng the great army attacked Muling Pass. Jisan laid an ambush at Getang Temple, caught the rebels off guard, cut through the pass and entered, burned it, and also broke the rebel nest at Liulang Bridge — in all these his merit ranked first; he was promoted to regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, as the main force assaulted Muling Pass, Jisan laid an ambush at Getang Temple, caught the rebels unawares, cut through the pass and set it ablaze, then smashed the rebel nest at Liulang Bridge — in each action his merit ranked first — and was promoted to regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十年，張國樑督諸軍攻江寧，季三任上關一路，壽德洲守賊秦禮國獻壘內應，破上關，拔出難民千餘，解散脅從五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zhang Guoliang directed the armies in the attack on Jiangning. Jisan held the upper pass route; Qin Liguo, a rebel holding Shoude Isle, offered his stockade as an inside contact; the upper pass was taken, more than a thousand refugees were pulled out, and more than five thousand coerced followers were released.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zhang Guoliang directed the armies against Jiangning. Jisan held the upper-pass route; Qin Liguo, a rebel holding Shoude Isle, offered his stockade as an inside contact; the upper pass fell, more than a thousand refugees were brought out, and more than five thousand coerced followers were released.

sentences.zh: 從張玉良援浙江，克餘杭、臨安，進秩提督。

translations.literal: Following Zhang Yuliang to relieve Zhejiang, he took Yuhang and Lin'an and was advanced to provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with Zhang Yuliang to relieve Zhejiang, he captured Yuhang and Lin'an and was advanced to provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，賊陷嚴州，掠富陽，季三孤軍往援，戰竟日，死之。

translations.literal: That autumn the rebels took Yanzhou and plundered Fuyang; Jisan went to the relief with a lone army, fought all day, and died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the rebels seized Yanzhou and plundered Fuyang; Jisan went alone to their relief, fought through the day, and fell.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He was granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant and given the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant and honored with the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 雙來，徐氏，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Shuang Lai, of the Xu clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang Lai, of the Xu clan, was a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 由拜唐阿累遷鑾儀衛治儀正，出為甘肅碾伯營都司，擢秦州營游擊。

translations.literal: Starting as a Baitang'a, he rose through repeated promotions to Director of Ceremonial Standards in the Imperial Procession Guard, went out as battalion commander of the Nianbo garrison in Gansu, and was promoted to colonel of the Qinzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a Baitang'a, he rose step by step to Director of Ceremonial Standards in the Imperial Procession Guard, went out to serve as battalion commander of the Nianbo garrison in Gansu, and was promoted to colonel of the Qinzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年，赴援回疆，行至黑孜布依遇賊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he went to relieve the Western Regions; on the road at Heizi Buyi he met rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he marched to relieve the Western Regions; on the road at Heizi Buyi he met rebels.

sentences.zh: 兵少，被圍，相持十餘日。

translations.literal: His troops were few; he was surrounded and stalemate lasted more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were few; he was surrounded and the standoff lasted more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 援至，合力破賊。

translations.literal: Relief arrived and together they broke the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived, and together they routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 方圍急，賊塞水源以斷汲路，越日泉湧盈塘。

translations.literal: At the height of the siege the rebels blocked the water source to cut off the supply route; the next day a spring gushed forth and filled the pond.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the siege the rebels blocked the water source to cut off the supply of water; the next day a spring gushed forth and filled the pond.

sentences.zh: 宣宗聞之，嘉歎曰：「此將士忠義所感也！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it, he praised and sighed, saying: "This is inspired by the loyalty and righteousness of the officers and soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it, he praised and sighed, saying, "This is inspired by the loyalty and righteousness of the officers and soldiers!"

sentences.zh: 命以參將用，賜花翎、法福哩巴圖魯勇號。

translations.literal: He ordered that Shuang Lai be employed as a regimental adjutant and granted the peacock feather and the honorific title Fafuri Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shuang Lai appointed regimental adjutant and bestowed on him the peacock feather and the honorific title Fafuri Baturol.

sentences.zh: 尋敗賊於駱駝脖子，加副將銜。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he defeated the rebels at Luotuo Bozi and was given the brevet rank of brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he defeated the rebels at Luotuo Bozi and received the brevet rank of brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 歷靈州營參將、永固協副將。

translations.literal: He served successively as regimental adjutant of the Lingzhou garrison and deputy regional commander of the Yonggu command.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as regimental adjutant of the Lingzhou garrison and deputy regional commander of the Yonggu command.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調赴欽差大臣琦善軍，擢肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Imperial Commissioner Qi Shan's army and was promoted to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Imperial Commissioner Qi Shan's army and promoted to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 三年，從琦善攻揚州，勇銳為一軍之冠，戰輒手執大旗以先，迭破賊，毀西北隅土城，悉奪其營壘。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Qi Shan in attacking Yangzhou. In bravery and dash he stood foremost in the army; in every battle he personally carried the great banner at the head, repeatedly broke the rebels, destroyed the earthen wall at the northwest corner, and seized all their camps and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Qi Shan in the assault on Yangzhou. In courage and dash he stood foremost in the army; in every battle he personally bore the great banner at the head, repeatedly broke the rebels, destroyed the earthen wall at the northwest corner, and seized all their camps and stockades.

sentences.zh: 賊遁入城死守，圍攻兩閱月。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into the city and held it to the death; the siege lasted two months.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew into the city and held it to the death; the siege lasted two months.

sentences.zh: 雙來發砲壞城垣丈餘，作桴渡河，逼城布雲梯，鼓勇先登，縱火，賊於城上苦鬥，槍彈如雨。

translations.literal: Shuang Lai opened fire with cannon and breached more than a zhang of wall, built rafts to cross the river, pressed up to the walls and deployed scaling ladders, roused his men to lead the ascent, and set fires. On the walls the rebels fought bitterly, and bullets fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang Lai's cannon fire breached more than a zhang of wall; he built rafts to cross the river, pressed to the walls with scaling ladders, roused his men to lead the climb, and set fires. On the ramparts the rebels fought desperately while bullets fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 雙來傷頰，折二齒，暈跌，扶下，從卒多傷亡，以無繼援而退。

translations.literal: Shuang Lai was wounded in the cheek, two teeth were broken, and he fainted and fell; he was helped down. Many of his followers were killed or wounded, and with no reinforcements to follow they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang Lai was wounded in the cheek and two teeth were broken; he fainted and fell and had to be helped down. Many of his followers were killed or wounded, and with no reinforcements to follow they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 特詔褒獎，加提督銜，他將觀望者並被譴。

translations.literal: A special edict praised and rewarded him, added the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief, and censured the other generals who had held back.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict praised and rewarded him, added the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief, and censured the other generals who had hung back.

sentences.zh: 越旬日，雙來复督隊攻城，力戰逾時，中砲，洞穿右股，猶大呼登城殺賊。

translations.literal: More than ten days later Shuang Lai again led his troops in assaulting the city. After fighting fiercely for a long time he was struck by cannon fire; the shot pierced his right thigh, yet he still shouted to scale the wall and kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later Shuang Lai again led his troops in storming the city. After long, fierce fighting he was hit by cannon fire; the shot tore through his right thigh, yet he still roared for his men to scale the wall and kill rebels.

sentences.zh: 翌日，創甚，卒於軍。

translations.literal: The next day his wounds were grave and he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his wounds proved mortal and he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 文宗素知其勇，事聞，震悼，手批其疏曰：「雙來何如是不幸？

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong had long known his bravery. When the report arrived, he was shaken with grief. In his own hand he wrote on the memorial: "How could Shuang Lai meet with such misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had long known his bravery. When the report arrived, he was shaken with grief. In his own hand he wrote on the memorial, "How could Shuang Lai meet with such misfortune?

sentences.zh: 朕隕涕覽奏，不勝悲憤！

translations.literal: Reading your memorial, I shed tears — I cannot contain my grief and indignation!
translations.idiomatic: Reading your memorial, I shed tears — my grief and indignation are beyond bearing!

sentences.zh: 然視彼貪生退縮者，奚啻霄壤。」

translations.literal: Yet compared with those who covet life and shrink back, the difference is as heaven from earth."
translations.idiomatic: Yet set beside those who cling to life and shrink from battle, the distance between them is as heaven from earth."

sentences.zh: 詔依提督例優恤，賜銀一千兩，命柩歸時專奏入城治喪，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: An edict granted favorably according to provincial commander-in-chief precedent, awarded one thousand taels of silver, ordered that when the coffin returned a special memorial be submitted for entry into the city to conduct the funeral, granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and gave the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted favorably according to provincial commander-in-chief precedent, awarded one thousand taels of silver, ordered that when the coffin returned a special memorial be submitted for entry into the city to conduct the funeral, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored him with the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 後都統德興阿疏言雙來與總兵瞿騰龍戰績尤異，先後於江北陣亡，請在揚州建雙忠祠合祀，詔允之。

translations.literal: Later Commandant Dexing'a memorialized that Shuang Lai and the regional commander Qu Tenglong had especially distinguished battle records and had both fallen in battle north of the Yangtze; he requested that a Twin Loyalty Shrine be built at Yangzhou for their joint enshrinement, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later Commandant Dexing'a memorialized that Shuang Lai and regional commander Qu Tenglong had especially distinguished themselves in battle and had both fallen north of the Yangtze; he asked that a Twin Loyalty Shrine be built at Yangzhou for their joint worship, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 瞿騰龍，字在田，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Qu Tenglong, courtesy name Zaitian, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tenglong, styled Zaitian, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍補千總，剿瑤匪趙金龍及乾州苗有功，累擢古丈坪營都司，署鎮筸鎮標游擊。

translations.literal: Starting in the ranks he was appointed company commander, suppressed the Yao bandit Zhao Jinlong and the Qianzhou Miao with merit, and through repeated promotions rose to battalion commander of the Guzhangping garrison and acting colonel of the Zhengang garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he was made company commander, helped suppress the Yao bandit Zhao Jinlong and the Qianzhou Miao, and through repeated promotion rose to battalion commander of the Guzhangping garrison and acting colonel of the Zhengang garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，率標兵赴廣西剿匪，迭破賊於武宣桐木、馬鞍山，永安古排塘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he led the garrison troops to Guangxi to suppress bandits and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Wuxuan Tongmu, Ma'an Shan, and Yong'an Gupaitang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he led the garrison troops to Guangxi to suppress bandits and repeatedly routed the enemy at Wuxuan Tongmu, Ma'an Shan, and Yong'an Gupaitang.

sentences.zh: 二年，援桂林，以巨砲擊賊於文昌門，殲斃甚眾，賜號莽阿巴圖魯，擢永綏協副將。

translations.literal: In the second year he went to relieve Guilin, used great cannon to strike the rebels at Wenchang Gate, killed and wounded a great many, was granted the title Mang'a Baturol, and was promoted to deputy regional commander of the Yongshui command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he went to relieve Guilin, used great cannon to strike the rebels at Wenchang Gate, killed and wounded a great many, was granted the honorific Mang'a Baturol, and was promoted to deputy regional commander of the Yongshui command.

sentences.zh: 追賊入湖南，迭戰於寧遠、耒陽、永興、安仁。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Hunan, he fought successive battles at Ningyuan, Leiyang, Yongxing, and Anren.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the rebels into Hunan, he fought a series of engagements at Ningyuan, Leiyang, Yongxing, and Anren.

sentences.zh: 賊圍攻長沙，騰龍率苗兵千人赴援，偕鄧紹良破南門外賊柵。

translations.literal: When the rebels besieged Changsha, Tenglong led a thousand Miao troops to the relief and, together with Deng Shaoliang, broke the rebel stockade outside the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged Changsha, Tenglong led a thousand Miao troops to the relief and, with Deng Shaoliang, broke the rebel stockade outside the south gate.

sentences.zh: 賊以地雷轟城，圮十餘丈，騰龍守城缺力禦，斬悍賊三百餘人，城复完，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: The rebels used a land mine to blast the wall, bringing down more than ten zhang. Tenglong held the breach and fought hard to repel them, beheaded more than three hundred fierce rebels, and the wall was made whole again; he was given regional commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blasted the wall with a land mine, bringing down more than ten zhang. Tenglong held the breach and fought them off, beheaded more than three hundred fierce rebels, and restored the wall; he was given regional commander rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，從向榮戰武昌，遂尾賊東下，擢湖北鄖陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Xiang Rong in fighting at Wuchang, then pursued the rebels eastward and was promoted to regional commander of the Yunyang garrison in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fought with Xiang Rong at Wuchang, then pursued the rebels eastward and was promoted to regional commander of the Yunyang garrison in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 抵江寧，賊已分黨北犯，命率所部馳赴山東、河南防剿。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangning the rebels had already divided their forces to raid north; he was ordered to lead his command in haste to Shandong and Henan to defend and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Jiangning the rebels had already split off a force to raid north; he was ordered to lead his command posthaste to Shandong and Henan to defend and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 行至高郵，琦善疏留其軍會攻揚州。

translations.literal: On the road at Gaoyou, Qi Shan memorialized to retain his army for the joint attack on Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoyou on the march, Qi Shan memorialized to keep his army for the joint attack on Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 騰龍身先士卒，與總兵雙來並號軍鋒。

translations.literal: Tenglong led from the front and, together with the regional commander Shuang Lai, was known as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tenglong always fought at the head of his men and, together with regional commander Shuang Lai, was hailed as the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 既而雙來以傷殞，遂兼領其軍，充翼長，琦善甚倚之。

translations.literal: Before long Shuang Lai died of his wounds; Tenglong then took joint command of his army, served as wing commander, and Qi Shan relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuang Lai died of his wounds; Tenglong then assumed joint command of his army, served as wing commander, and became one on whom Qi Shan leaned heavily.

sentences.zh: 揚州久不克，而賊之踞瓜洲者盡力來援。

translations.literal: Yangzhou long went untaken, while the rebels holding Guazhou exerted all their strength to come to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou remained untaken for a long time while the rebels holding Guazhou mustered every strength to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 騰龍扼三汊河，賊至，十倍我軍，騰龍下令「有進無退，回顧者斬」，下馬持大刀闖入陣，士卒皆喋血戰，賊退，夜乘雷雨突之，賊不辨眾寡，自相踐殺，及曉，屍骸狼藉，斃賊二千有奇。

translations.literal: Tenglong blocked the San Cha River. When the rebels arrived they outnumbered his army tenfold. Tenglong gave the order: "Advance only, never retreat — whoever looks back will be beheaded." He dismounted, took up a great sword, and charged into the formation; his soldiers all fought drenched in blood, the rebels withdrew, and at night he took advantage of thunder and rain to strike suddenly. The rebels could not tell friend from foe and trampled one another to death; by dawn corpses lay strewn everywhere, and more than two thousand rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tenglong blocked the San Cha River. When the rebels arrived they outnumbered his army ten to one. He gave the order: "Forward only — never retreat; whoever looks back will be beheaded." Dismounting, he seized a great sword and charged into the enemy line; his soldiers fought drenched in blood until the rebels withdrew. That night, using thunder and rain as cover, he struck suddenly; the rebels could not tell friend from foe and trampled one another to death. By dawn corpses lay everywhere, and more than two thousand rebels had been killed.

sentences.zh: 尋賊揚帆迳趨揚州南門，登東岸，复馳擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels set sail and made straight for Yangzhou's south gate, landing on the east bank; he again galloped to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels set sail straight for Yangzhou's south gate and landed on the east bank; he again galloped out, struck them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 於是樹巨椿以阻河路，城賊屢突圍，擊退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he planted great piles to block the river route; the rebels in the city repeatedly broke out, and each time he beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove great piles into the river to block the route; rebels inside the city broke out again and again, and each time he repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊全隊沖出，併入瓜洲，乃復郡城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the rebels broke out in full force and merged into Guazhou, and the prefectural city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebels broke out in full force, merged into Guazhou, and the prefectural city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 初，向榮疏調騰龍回軍江寧，不許。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiang Rong had memorialized to transfer Tenglong's army back to Jiangning, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiang Rong had memorialized to transfer Tenglong's army back to Jiangning, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 至是詔率兵援安慶，琦善奏三汊河要衝，恃騰龍力守，仍請留。

translations.literal: At this point an edict ordered him to lead troops to relieve Anqing, but Qi Shan memorialized that the San Cha River was a vital pass and depended on Tenglong's stout defense; he again requested that Tenglong be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered him to lead troops to relieve Anqing, but Qi Shan memorialized that the San Cha River was a vital choke point and depended on Tenglong's stout defense; he again asked that Tenglong be kept there.

sentences.zh: 賊於運河南岸築數壘以逼三汊河，進攻破之。

translations.literal: The rebels built several stockades on the south bank of the Grand Canal to press on the San Cha River; he advanced and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built several stockades on the south bank of the Grand Canal to press the San Cha River; he advanced and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，進攻瓜洲，設伏誘賊出，伏起，大破之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he advanced to attack Guazhou, set an ambush to lure the rebels out, and when the ambush rose he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he advanced against Guazhou, laid an ambush to draw the rebels out, and when the trap sprang inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 二月，復進攻，乘夜雪襲賊，連破二壘，深入，賊傾巢出，鈔官軍後，圍數重，戰竟日，被傷，下馬步戰，力竭死之，年六十有四。

translations.literal: In the second month he again advanced to attack. Taking advantage of night snow he raided the rebels, broke two stockades in succession, and pressed deep in; the rebels came out in full force, cut behind the government army, and surrounded them in layer upon layer. The battle lasted all day; he was wounded, dismounted to fight on foot, and died when his strength was spent, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he attacked again. Under cover of night snow he raided the rebels, broke two stockades in succession, and pressed deep inside; the rebels came out in full force, cut behind the government army, and surrounded them in ring after ring. The battle lasted all day; wounded, he dismounted to fight on foot and died when his strength gave out, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡威壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous title Weizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and honored with the posthumous title Formidable and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 王國才，字錦堂，原姓羅氏，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Wang Guocai, courtesy name Jintang, originally surnamed Luo, was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guocai, styled Jintang, originally bore the surname Luo and came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 以武舉效力督標，洊升守備。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he served in the provincial garrison standard and rose through repeated promotions to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: As a military licentiate he served in the provincial garrison standard and rose through repeated promotion to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 道光末，剿彌渡回匪，擒賊首海老陝，賜號胜勇巴圖魯，擢都司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign he suppressed the Midu Hui bandits, captured the bandit chieftain Hai Laoshan, was granted the title Shengyong Baturol, and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daoguang reign he suppressed the Midu Hui bandits, captured the bandit chieftain Hai Laoshan, was granted the honorific Shengyong Baturol, and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 從剿廣西賊，轉戰大黃江、永安州有功。

translations.literal: He followed in suppressing the Guangxi rebels and campaigned with merit at the Dahuang River and Yongan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Guangxi rebels and distinguished himself at the Dahuang River and in Yongan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋撤滇軍歸伍。

translations.literal: Soon the Yunnan army was withdrawn and the men returned to their units.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yunnan army was withdrawn and the men returned to their units.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，平尋甸回匪，擢山東青州參將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he pacified the Xundian Hui bandits and was promoted to regimental adjutant of Qingzhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he put down the Xundian Hui bandits and was raised to regimental adjutant of Qingzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三年，吳文鎔移督兩湖，疏調率所部赴湖北，行至天門，遇賊，以親兵七十人擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third year Wu Wenrong was transferred to governor-general of Huguang and memorialized to transfer Guocai to lead his command to Hubei. On the road at Tianmen he met rebels and with seventy personal guards drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wu Wenrong was transferred to governor-general of Huguang and memorialized to have Guocai lead his command to Hubei. On the road at Tianmen he met rebels and, with seventy personal guards, put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 會文鎔戰歿黃梅，國才將返滇，過荊州，將軍官文留之，予兵千二百、練勇五百，守城北龍會橋。

translations.literal: When Wenrong was killed in battle at Huangmei, Guocai was about to return to Yunnan. Passing through Jingzhou, the commandant Guan Wen retained him, gave him twelve hundred soldiers and five hundred trained militia, and ordered him to hold Longhui Bridge north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenrong was killed in battle at Huangmei, Guocai was about to return to Yunnan. Passing through Jingzhou, Commandant Guan Wen kept him there, gave him twelve hundred soldiers and five hundred trained militia, and ordered him to hold Longhui Bridge north of the city.

sentences.zh: 賊萬餘猝至，軍士氣沮，國才曰：「賊如潮湧，不進何以求生！」

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rebels arrived suddenly; the soldiers' spirit sank. Guocai said: "The rebels surge like a tide — how can we survive unless we advance!"
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand rebels arrived suddenly; the soldiers' spirit sank. Guocai said, "The rebels surge like a tide — how can we survive unless we advance!"

sentences.zh: 親以鳥槍斃執旗賊，大呼陷陣，賊披靡，墜河無算。

translations.literal: He personally used his musket to shoot down the flag bearer, shouted and plunged into the enemy line; the rebels scattered, and countless fell into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He himself shot down the flag bearer with his musket, shouted, and plunged into the enemy line; the rebels broke and fled, and untold numbers fell into the river.

sentences.zh: 追至馬湟山，賊敗竄，軍中稱其勇。

translations.literal: Pursuing them to Mahuang Shan, the rebels were defeated and fled; the army praised his bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Mahuang Shan, he routed the rebels and put them to flight; the army acclaimed his valor.

sentences.zh: 官文令整飭諸縣團練，荊州獲安，賜花翎，以副將升用。

translations.literal: Guan Wen ordered him to reorganize the local militia in the various counties; Jingzhou was secured, he was granted the peacock feather, and was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen ordered him to reorganize the county militia; Jingzhou was secured, he received the peacock feather, and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，署督標中軍副將，從總督楊霈防德安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served as acting deputy brigade commander of the provincial garrison's central battalion and followed Governor-General Yang Piao in defending Dean.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he acted as deputy brigade commander of the provincial garrison's central battalion and marched with Governor-General Yang Piao to defend Dean.

sentences.zh: 會湘軍規大冶，國才當右路，連破賊，克蘄州。

translations.literal: When the Hunan Army planned to take Daye, Guocai held the right route, repeatedly broke the rebels, and took Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hunan Army planned to take Daye, Guocai held the right wing, repeatedly routed the rebels, and captured Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 楊霈以川練千人益其軍，進攻九江。

translations.literal: Yang Piao added a thousand Sichuan militia to his army and advanced to attack Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Piao reinforced his army with a thousand Sichuan militia, and they advanced against Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，率部將畢金科戰城下，數捷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he led his subordinate officer Bi Jinke to fight below the walls and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he led his subordinate Bi Jinke in fighting below the walls and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 會揚霈師潰，國才回援武昌，夜至，城已陷，未知也；

translations.literal: When Yang Piao's army collapsed, Guocai returned to relieve Wuchang and arrived at night; the city had already fallen, though he did not yet know it;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Piao's army collapsed, Guocai turned back to relieve Wuchang and arrived at night; the city had already fallen, though he did not yet know it;

sentences.zh: 先驅入城，始覺。

translations.literal: the vanguard entered the city before he realized it.
translations.idiomatic: his vanguard entered the city before the truth dawned on him.

sentences.zh: 賊由漢陽悉眾來拒，國才突圍出，駐金口，進大軍山。

translations.literal: The rebels from Hanyang came out in full force to resist; Guocai broke through the encirclement, encamped at Jinkou, and advanced to Dashan Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels from Hanyang came out in full strength to oppose him; Guocai broke through the encirclement, encamped at Jinkou, and advanced to Dashan Hill.

sentences.zh: 尋屯沌口，偕水師合攻漢陽，設伏誘賊出，殲之。

translations.literal: Soon he encamped at Zhunkou, joined the naval forces in a joint attack on Hanyang, set an ambush to lure the rebels out, and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he encamped at Zhunkou, joined the fleet in a combined assault on Hanyang, laid an ambush to draw the rebels out, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 賊屢襲金口、沌口，皆擊退。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly raided Jinkou and Zhunkou, and each time he beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels repeatedly raided Jinkou and Zhunkou, and each time he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 破大別山賊壘，授竹山協副將，署鄖陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He broke the rebel stockade on Mount Dabie, was appointed deputy regional commander of the Zhushan command, and served as acting regional commander of the Yunyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed the rebel stockade on Mount Dabie, received appointment as deputy regional commander of the Zhushan command, and acted as regional commander of the Yunyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 總督官文進逼漢陽，國才屢從破賊。

translations.literal: Governor-General Guan Wen pressed the attack on Hanyang, and Guocai repeatedly followed in breaking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor-General Guan Wen pressed the attack on Hanyang, Guocai again and again helped break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 六年，諸軍合攻，國才越壕逼城下，一擁而入，巷戰，殺賊甚眾，加總兵銜，記名簡放。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the various armies joined in the attack; Guocai crossed the moat and pressed to the foot of the wall, surged in at once, fought in the streets, and killed a great many rebels; he was given regional commander rank and registered for appointment by name when a vacancy occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the allied armies attacked together; Guocai crossed the moat to the foot of the wall, surged inside at once, fought through the streets, and killed a great many rebels; he received regional commander rank and was registered for appointment by name when a vacancy opened.

sentences.zh: 复黃梅，守之，改隸將軍都興阿。

translations.literal: He recovered Huangmei and garrisoned it, then was transferred to the command of Commandant Duxing'a.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Huangmei and garrisoned it, then passed to the command of Commandant Duxing'a.

sentences.zh: 七年，賊由太湖來犯，以空城誘賊入，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: In the seventh year rebels came from Taihu to raid; he used an empty city to lure the rebels in and killed and captured them without number.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year rebels came from Taihu to raid; he left the city empty to lure them in and killed and captured them beyond count.

sentences.zh: 追至九江對岸，連破賊段窯、楓樹坳、狗山鎮。

translations.literal: Pursuing them to the opposite bank of Jiujiang, he broke the rebels in succession at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, and Goushan Town.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to the opposite bank of Jiujiang, he routed the rebels in succession at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, and Goushan Town.

sentences.zh: 雲南迴匪熾，調回援，官文、胡林翼疏留不遣。

translations.literal: The Yunnan Hui rebels flared up fiercely and he was transferred back to relieve them, but Guan Wen and Hu Linji memorialized to retain him and he was not sent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yunnan Hui rebels flared up he was ordered back to relieve them, but Guan Wen and Hu Linji memorialized to keep him and he was not sent.

sentences.zh: 黃梅城僻隘，國才謂不足屏蔽，請守雙林驛。

translations.literal: Huangmei city was remote and cramped; Guocai said it was insufficient to serve as a shield and requested to hold Shuanglin Post instead.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmei city was remote and cramped; Guocai argued it could not serve as an effective shield and asked instead to hold Shuanglin Post.

sentences.zh: 都興阿不許，乃屯城西，分副將石清吉守城，賊屢犯，卻之，授貴州安義鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Duxing'a would not agree; he therefore encamped west of the city and detached the deputy brigade commander Shi Qingji to hold the city. The rebels repeatedly attacked and were repulsed; he was appointed regional commander of the Anyi garrison in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duxing'a refused; Guocai therefore encamped west of the city and detached Deputy Brigade Commander Shi Qingji to hold the walls. The rebels attacked again and again and were repulsed; he was appointed regional commander of the Anyi garrison in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，皖賊陳玉成糾賊數十萬上犯，國才被圍，力戰，歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Anhui rebel Chen Yucheng gathered several hundred thousand rebels for a great northern raid; Guocai was surrounded, fought hard, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Anhui rebel Chen Yucheng gathered several hundred thousand men for a great northern raid; Guocai was surrounded, fought to the end, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，建專祠，諡剛介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, given a dedicated shrine, and given the posthumous title Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made provincial commander-in-chief, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, given a dedicated shrine, and honored with the posthumous title Steadfast and Upright.

sentences.zh: 虎坤元，字子厚，四川成都人。

translations.literal: Hu Kunyuan, courtesy name Zihou, was a native of Chengdu in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kunyuan, styled Zihou, came from Chengdu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 父嵩林，咸豐初，以湖南游擊調廣西剿匪，從向榮戰紫荊山，攻永安，解桂林、長沙圍，並有功。

translations.literal: His father Songlin, at the beginning of Xianfeng, was transferred from Hunan colonel to Guangxi to suppress bandits; he followed Xiang Rong in fighting at Zijing Shan, attacking Yong'an, and lifting the sieges of Guilin and Changsha, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Songlin, at the opening of the Xianfeng reign, was transferred from Hunan colonel to Guangxi to suppress bandits; he followed Xiang Rong at Zijing Shan, in the attack on Yong'an, and in lifting the sieges of Guilin and Changsha, earning merit in each.

sentences.zh: 從至江南，累擢湖北宜昌鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Following him to Jiangnan, he rose through repeated promotions to regional commander of the Yichang garrison in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Following him to Jiangnan, he rose through repeated promotion to regional commander of the Yichang garrison in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫吉爾杭阿克上海，遂從攻鎮江，屢破賊於寶蓋山、倉頭、下蜀街、高資。

translations.literal: Together with Provincial Governor Geleing'a he went to Shanghai, then followed in the attack on Zhenjiang and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Baogai Shan, Cangtou, Xiasu Street, and Gaozi.
translations.idiomatic: With Provincial Governor Geleing'a he went to Shanghai, then joined the attack on Zhenjiang and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Baogai Shan, Cangtou, Xiasu Street, and Gaozi.

sentences.zh: 在江南軍中稱宿將。

translations.literal: In the Jiangnan army he was known as a veteran commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan army he was regarded as a seasoned veteran.

sentences.zh: 坤元，年十七，從父軍，勇力過人，戰輒先登，軍中號曰「小虎」。

translations.literal: Kunyuan, at seventeen, followed his father's army. His courage and strength surpassed others; in every battle he was first to scale the walls, and the army called him "Little Tiger."
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan was seventeen when he joined his father's command. His courage and strength outmatched others; in every fight he was first over the wall, and the army nicknamed him "Little Tiger."

sentences.zh: 初至江寧，奪鍾山賊壘，功最，擢守備。

translations.literal: When he first reached Jiangning he seized the rebel stockade on Bell Mountain; his merit ranked foremost and he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached Jiangning he seized the rebel stockade on Bell Mountain; his merit ranked first and he was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，克高淳、太平，賜花翎、鼓勇巴圖魯勇號，擢川北鎮標都司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took Gaochun and Taiping, was granted the peacock feather and the honorific title Guyong Baturol, and was promoted to battalion commander of the North Sichuan garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he captured Gaochun and Taiping, received the peacock feather and the honorific title Guyong Baturol, and was promoted to battalion commander of the North Sichuan garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 五年，援灣沚，焚賊舟，乘勝取蕪湖，坤元躍登城，殺守陴賊，遂克之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went to relieve Wanzhi, burned the rebel boats, and pressed the advantage to take Wuhu; Kunyuan leaped onto the wall, killed the defenders on the ramparts, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he went to relieve Wanzhi, burned the rebel boats, and pressed the advantage to take Wuhu; Kunyuan leaped onto the wall, killed the defenders on the ramparts, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 六年，江寧賊出援鎮江，坤元元旦馳至三汊河，擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jiangning rebels came out to relieve Zhenjiang; on New Year's Day Kunyuan galloped to the San Cha River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Jiangning rebels came out to relieve Zhenjiang; on New Year's Day Kunyuan raced to the San Cha River and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又戰於下蜀街，破賊壘，追賊直至仙鶴門，擢建昌鎮標游擊。

translations.literal: He again fought at Xiasu Street, broke the rebel stockade, pursued the rebels all the way to Xianhe Gate, and was promoted to colonel of the Jianchang garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Xiasu Street, broke the rebel stockade, pursued the enemy all the way to Xianhe Gate, and was promoted to colonel of the Jianchang garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 從總兵秦如虎援浙江，而寧國告陷，遇賊於宣城紅林橋，設伏，身率數騎誘賊，敗之。

translations.literal: He followed the regional commander Qin Ruhu to relieve Zhejiang, but Ningguo reported fallen; he met the rebels at Honglin Bridge in Xuancheng, set an ambush, and personally led a few horsemen to lure the rebels and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed regional commander Qin Ruhu to relieve Zhejiang, but word came that Ningguo had fallen; at Honglin Bridge in Xuancheng he met the rebels, laid an ambush, and personally led a handful of horsemen to lure them into defeat.

sentences.zh: 進攻寧國未下，回援鎮江，嵩林為賊所困，馳入重圍掖之出。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Ningguo but did not take it, then returned to relieve Zhenjiang; Songlin was trapped by the rebels, and he galloped into the heavy encirclement to bring him out.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Ningguo but failed to take it, then turned back to relieve Zhenjiang; Songlin was trapped by the rebels, and he galloped into the heavy encirclement to bring him out.

sentences.zh: 會江南大營潰，向榮等退守丹陽，賊躡至，勢甚張，坤元偕張國樑力戰卻之。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed, Xiang Rong and the others fell back to defend Danyang; the rebels pursued and their momentum was very strong. Kunyuan and Zhang Guoliang fought hard and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed, Xiang Rong and the others fell back to defend Danyang; the pursuing rebels were in full flood. Kunyuan and Zhang Guoliang fought hard and threw them back.

sentences.zh: 遂從嵩林移駐珥陵，扼賊犯常州之路。

translations.literal: He then followed Songlin in moving his encampment to Erling and blocked the route by which the rebels might invade Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Songlin in moving camp to Erling and blocked the route by which the rebels might strike Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，國樑戰五里牌，傷胯，急召坤元夜至，簡精銳，未曉即出，逾簡瀆河，東攻黃土台賊壘，躍上壘牆，毀其柵，大隊擁入，勁騎鈔截，賊無脫者，連破五壘。

translations.literal: Before long Guoliang fought at Wulipai and was wounded in the hip; he urgently summoned Kunyuan, who came by night, picked elite troops, and marched out before dawn. Crossing the Jianlu River he attacked the rebel stockade at Huangtu Terrace from the east, leaped onto the stockade wall, destroyed the palisade, and the main force surged in; fierce cavalry cut off the retreat, and not one rebel escaped; five stockades were taken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guoliang fought at Wulipai and was wounded in the hip; he urgently summoned Kunyuan, who came by night, picked elite troops, and marched out before dawn. Crossing the Jianlu River he attacked the rebel stockade at Huangtu Terrace from the east, leaped onto the stockade wall, tore down the palisade, and the main force poured in; fierce cavalry cut off retreat so that not one rebel escaped, and five stockades fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 國樑亦破河西賊壘，賊勢始挫。

translations.literal: Guoliang also broke the rebel stockade west of the river, and the rebels' momentum was checked for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang also broke the rebel stockade west of the river, and for the first time the rebels' momentum faltered.

sentences.zh: 坤元以是名出諸將上，乘勝進兵，踰月遂解金壇之圍，擢參將。

translations.literal: Because of this Kunyuan's fame rose above the other generals; pressing the advantage he advanced, and within a month the siege of Jintan was lifted; he was promoted to regimental adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: This feat lifted Kunyuan's name above the other generals; pressing his advantage he advanced, and within a month the siege of Jintan was lifted; he was promoted to regimental adjutant.

sentences.zh: 進攻東壩，填壕登城，負創力戰，手斬悍賊，復之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Dongba, filled the moat and scaled the wall, fought hard though wounded, and with his own hand beheaded a fierce rebel; the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Dongba, filled the moat and scaled the wall, fought on though wounded, and with his own hand beheaded a fierce rebel; the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 又克高淳，以副將侭先升用。

translations.literal: He again took Gaochun and was promoted to brigade commander ahead of others in seniority.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Gaochun again and was promoted to brigade commander ahead of others in seniority.

sentences.zh: 七年，會攻溧水。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he joined in the attack on Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined the assault on Lishui.

sentences.zh: 賊屢來援，與城賊夾攻官軍。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly came to the relief and, together with the rebels in the city, attacked the government army from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns came again and again, and together with the rebels inside the city they attacked the government army from both sides.

sentences.zh: 坤元迭破之於鄔山、拓塘、博望、天里山、小茅山，凡十餘戰，殲戮無算，擒偽迓天侯陳士章，鏖斗城下四晝夜，躍登南門，复溧水，授貴州定廣協副將。

translations.literal: Kunyuan repeatedly defeated them at Wu Shan, Tuotang, Bowang, Tianli Shan, and Xiaomao Shan — more than ten battles in all — killing and capturing without number, capturing the false Yingtian Marquis Chen Shizhang, fought fiercely below the walls for four days and four nights, leaped onto the south gate, recovered Lishui, and was appointed deputy regional commander of the Dingguang command in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan repeatedly defeated them at Wu Shan, Tuotang, Bowang, Tianli Shan, and Xiaomao Shan — more than ten battles in all — killing and capturing beyond count, taking the false Yingtian Marquis Chen Shizhang, fighting fiercely below the walls for four days and four nights, leaping onto the south gate, retaking Lishui, and receiving appointment as deputy regional commander of the Dingguang command in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊於高陽橋，克湖墅、龍都。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Gaoyang Bridge and took Hushu and Longdu.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels again at Gaoyang Bridge and captured Hushu and Longdu.

sentences.zh: 張國樑攻句容，賊堅守未下，檄坤元往助。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang attacked Jurong, but the rebels held firm and the city was not taken; an order was sent for Kunyuan to go and assist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang attacked Jurong, but the rebels held firm and the city would not fall; an order went out for Kunyuan to assist.

sentences.zh: 值賊出撲，率數十騎突之，進逼南門，縱火焚城樓，大軍繼之，遂克句容。

translations.literal: Just as the rebels came out to strike, he led several dozen horsemen in a sudden charge, pressed up to the south gate, set fire and burned the gate tower, the main army followed, and Jurong was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the rebels sallied forth, he led several dozen horsemen in a sudden charge, pressed to the south gate, set fire to the gate tower, and with the main army following took Jurong.

sentences.zh: 敘功，以總兵記名簡放。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was registered for appointment as regional commander by name.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were assessed he was registered for appointment as regional commander by name.

sentences.zh: 從國樑規鎮江，時賊由江寧來援，蟻聚七星觀、倉頭。

translations.literal: He followed Guoliang in planning the attack on Zhenjiang. At that time rebels from Jiangning came to the relief and swarmed like ants at Qixing Guan and Cangtou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guoliang in planning the attack on Zhenjiang. At that time rebels from Jiangning came to the relief and swarmed thick as ants at Qixing Guan and Cangtou.

sentences.zh: 坤元以輕騎誘敵入伏中，大敗之，追擊，立破三壘。

translations.literal: Kunyuan used light cavalry to lure the enemy into an ambush and inflicted a great defeat; pursuing, he immediately broke three stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan used light cavalry to lure the enemy into an ambush and inflicted a great defeat; in pursuit he immediately broke three stockades.

sentences.zh: 賊退至三汊河，伏兵又起，無去路。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated to the San Cha River; the ambush rose again, and there was no way out.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to the San Cha River; the ambush rose again, and they had nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 坤元大呼：「棄戈者免死！

translations.literal: Kunyuan shouted loudly: "Those who cast aside their weapons shall be spared!
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan shouted at the top of his voice, "Those who cast aside their weapons shall be spared!

sentences.zh: 殺賊首者賞！」

translations.literal: Those who kill rebel chiefs shall be rewarded!"
