translations.idiomatic: Reward whoever kills a rebel chief!"

sentences.zh: 降者數百人。

translations.literal: Several hundred surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred laid down their arms.

sentences.zh: 是役斬馘及淹斃者三千有奇，生擒三百。

translations.literal: In this battle those beheaded, drowned, and killed exceeded three thousand; three hundred were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle those beheaded, drowned, or otherwise killed exceeded three thousand; three hundred were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 尋敗賊於西堰岡，援賊复於倉頭、顧家壩築壘。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he defeated the rebels at Xiyan Hill; relief rebels again built stockades at Cangtou and Gujia Dam.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he defeated the rebels at Xiyan Hill; relief rebels then rebuilt stockades at Cangtou and Gujia Dam.

sentences.zh: 坤元於山後樹幟為疑兵，自率小隊沖鋒，殪悍賊。

translations.literal: Kunyuan planted banners behind the hill as a feint and personally led a small detachment in a charge, killing fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan planted banners behind the hill as a feint and personally led a small detachment in a charge that killed many fierce rebels.

sentences.zh: 而賊以大隊來拒，諸軍環擊，乘勢全毀賊營，鎮江守賊遂遁。

translations.literal: When the rebels came in force to resist, the various units closed in from all sides, took advantage of the momentum to destroy the rebel camps entirely, and the rebels holding Zhenjiang fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came in force to resist, the allied units closed in from every side, seized the momentum to destroy the rebel camps entirely, and the garrison at Zhenjiang fled.

sentences.zh: 追至龍潭，痛殲之。

translations.literal: Pursuing them to Longtan, he annihilated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Longtan, he cut them down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 坤元甫授直隸通永鎮總兵，文宗手批其謝恩疏曰：「聞汝父子在軍營甚為奮勇。

translations.literal: Kunyuan had just been appointed regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili when Emperor Wenzong wrote in his own hand on the memorial of thanks: "I have heard that you and your father have fought with great valor in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyuan had just been appointed regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili when Emperor Wenzong wrote in his own hand on the memorial of thanks, "I have heard that you and your father have fought with great valor in camp.

sentences.zh: 汝年未三十，已膺顯秩。

translations.literal: You are not yet thirty and have already received a distinguished rank.
translations.idiomatic: You are not yet thirty and already hold high rank.

sentences.zh: 務自勉勵，以副朕望。」

translations.literal: Strive to encourage yourself, that you may fulfill my hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself to the utmost, that you may answer to my expectations."

sentences.zh: 至是復下部優敘。

translations.literal: At this point the ministry again issued a favorable commendation.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the ministry again issued a commendation in his favor.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，奪情留軍。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he entered mourning for his mother, but was retained in the army despite the mourning obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother but was kept with the army despite the mourning obligation.

sentences.zh: 八年，攻秣陵關，逼賊巢為壘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attacked Muling Pass and pressed the rebel nest into a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he attacked Muling Pass and pressed the rebel stronghold into a fortified stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊出鬥，敗之，窮追，單騎獨前，惟游擊劉萬清從，疑有伏，止之，勿聽，進至石橋，中槍而殞，萬清奪其屍還。

translations.literal: The rebels came out to fight; he defeated them and pursued relentlessly, riding alone at the front with only the guerrilla colonel Liu Wanqing following. Suspecting an ambush, Wanqing tried to stop him, but he would not listen; advancing to Stone Bridge he was struck by a musket ball and fell. Wanqing seized his body and brought it back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to fight; he defeated them and pursued without stopping, riding alone at the front with only guerrilla colonel Liu Wanqing behind him. Suspecting an ambush, Wanqing tried to halt him, but he would not listen; at Stone Bridge a musket ball struck him down. Wanqing recovered his body and brought it back.

sentences.zh: 和春疏聞，言：「坤元從軍八載，忠勇性成。

translations.literal: When He Chun's memorial arrived, he said: "Kunyuan served in the army for eight years; loyalty and courage were inborn in him.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chun's memorial arrived, he said, "Kunyuan served in the army for eight years; loyalty and courage were inborn in him.

sentences.zh: 善以少擊眾，自為都守。

translations.literal: He was skilled at defeating many with few and commanded in his own right.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at beating larger forces with fewer men and commanded armies in his own right.

sentences.zh: 父子所入之貲，悉以養勇士。

translations.literal: All the wealth that he and his father put into the army was used entirely to support brave men.
translations.idiomatic: Every coin he and his father invested in the army went to support brave fighters.

sentences.zh: 故旌旗所指，無不披靡。

translations.literal: Thus wherever his banners pointed, none failed to be swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his banners turned, the enemy gave way.

sentences.zh: 歷經頒給御賜金牌六次，受二等傷四次，頭等傷十二次。

translations.literal: He had been granted the imperially bestowed gold medal six times, received second-class wounds four times, and first-class wounds twelve times.
translations.idiomatic: The throne had bestowed on him the imperial gold medal six times; he had suffered four second-class wounds and twelve first-class wounds.

sentences.zh: 灼頸落指，瀕死者屢矣。

translations.literal: His neck was burned, fingers were lost, and he had repeatedly been at death's door.
translations.idiomatic: His neck had been burned, fingers lost — again and again he had brushed death.

sentences.zh: 既歿，大江南北同聲悼惜。」

translations.literal: After his death, north and south of the Yangtze alike mourned him with one voice."
translations.idiomatic: After his death, voices north and south of the Yangtze mourned him as one."

sentences.zh: 詔從優恤，於溧水、湖墅及死事地方建專祠，諡忠壯，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict granted favorable posthumous honors; dedicated shrines were built at Lishui, Hushu, and the place where he died; he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang and the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted favorable posthumous honors; dedicated shrines were built at Lishui, Hushu, and the place where he died; he was honored with the posthumous title Loyal and Robust and granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 未娶無子，以弟坤岡襲。

translations.literal: He had not married and had no son; his younger brother Kun'gang succeeded to the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He had never married and left no son; his younger brother Kun'gang inherited the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 是年，其父嵩林守溧水，為賊陷，坐褫職，以坤元陣亡故，獲免治罪。

translations.literal: That year his father Songlin was holding Lishui when it fell to the rebels; he was dismissed from office for the offense, but because Kunyuan had fallen in battle he was spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That year his father Songlin was holding Lishui when it fell to the rebels; he was dismissed for the offense, but because Kunyuan had died in battle he was spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 嵩林回籍助剿滇匪，命襄治團練，尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Songlin returned to his native place to assist in suppressing the Yunnan bandits; he was ordered to help administer the local militia and soon died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin returned home to help suppress the Yunnan bandits, was ordered to help administer the local militia, and soon died there.

sentences.zh: 戴文英，廣東羅定人。

translations.literal: Dai Wenying was a native of Luoding in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Wenying came from Luoding in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 由行伍從剿羅鏡凌十八有功，擢千總。

translations.literal: Starting in the ranks he followed in suppressing the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba with merit and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he helped suppress the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba, earned merit, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，從向榮援江寧。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Xiang Rong to relieve Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he marched with Xiang Rong to relieve Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 初至進攻，文英偕張國樑穿越深林叢葦十餘處，潛襲雨花台賊營後，大敗之，賜號色固巴圖魯。

translations.literal: On first arriving he joined the assault; Wenying, together with Zhang Guoliang, passed through more than ten tracts of deep forest and reed marsh, secretly struck the rear of the rebel camp at Yuhuatai, and inflicted a great defeat; he was granted the honorific title Segu Baturol.
translations.idiomatic: On first arriving he joined the assault; Wenying and Zhang Guoliang passed through more than ten tracts of deep forest and reed marsh, struck the rear of the rebel camp at Yuhuatai by surprise, and inflicted a crushing defeat; he received the honorific title Segu Baturol.

sentences.zh: 四年，勦賊七橋甕，往來衝鋒，又偕總兵德安破賊營。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he suppressed the rebels at Qiqiao Weng, charging back and forth in battle, and again, together with the regional commander De An, broke the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he suppressed the rebels at Qiqiao Weng, charging back and forth in the fight, and again, with regional commander De An, broke the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 五年，戰高資，皆以勇銳稱，累擢惠州營都司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fought at Gaozi; in all cases he was praised for courage and dash, and through repeated promotions he rose to battalion commander of the Huizhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fought at Gaozi; everywhere he was praised for courage and dash, and through repeated promotion he rose to battalion commander of the Huizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 六年，攻鎮江，戰於京峴山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he attacked Zhenjiang and fought at Jingxian Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the assault on Zhenjiang and battled at Jingxian Shan.

sentences.zh: 馳馬入賊陣，槍斃悍賊甚多，擢南詔營游擊。

translations.literal: Galloping into the rebel formation, he shot down many fierce rebels with his musket and was promoted to guerrilla colonel of the Nanzhao garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Galloping into the rebel ranks, he shot down many fierce rebels with his musket and was promoted to guerrilla colonel of the Nanzhao garrison.

sentences.zh: 從張國樑援金壇，率精銳過河奮擊，解金壇之圍。

translations.literal: Following Zhang Guoliang to relieve Jintan, he led elite troops across the river in a fierce assault and lifted the siege of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhang Guoliang to relieve Jintan, he led elite troops across the river in a fierce assault and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督怡良薦舉將才，文英與其選。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yi Liang of the Two Jiangs recommended men of generalship; Wenying was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yi Liang of the Two Jiangs recommended men of generalship, and Wenying was among those chosen.

sentences.zh: 大兵克東壩賊壘，平寶堰賊巢，文英率茅村團練獨當一路，斬獲多，擢淮安營參將。

translations.literal: When the main army took the rebel stockade at Dongba and leveled the rebel nest at Baoyan, Wenying led the Maocun militia alone on one route, killed and captured a great many, and was promoted to regimental adjutant of the Huai'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army took the rebel stockade at Dongba and leveled the nest at Baoyan, Wenying led the Maocun militia alone on one route, killed and captured a great many, and was promoted to regimental adjutant of the Huai'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，從張國樑攻鎮江，駐紅花山。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Zhang Guoliang in attacking Zhenjiang and encamped at Honghua Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he campaigned with Zhang Guoliang against Zhenjiang and took position at Honghua Shan.

sentences.zh: 賊眾來撲，文英衝入賊中，手刺殺悍酋數人，賊大敗，擢江南督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: When a great rebel force came to strike, Wenying charged into their midst and with his own hand stabbed and killed several fierce chiefs; the rebels suffered a great defeat, and he was promoted to deputy brigade commander of the Jiangnan governor's central battalion.
translations.idiomatic: When a great rebel force came to strike, Wenying charged into their midst and with his own hand stabbed several fierce chiefs to death; the rebels suffered a crushing defeat, and he was promoted to deputy brigade commander of the Jiangnan governor's central battalion.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，攻克鎮江府城，記名總兵。

translations.literal: That winter the prefectural city of Zhenjiang was taken, and he was registered for appointment as regional commander by name.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhenjiang's prefectural city fell, and his name was entered for appointment as regional commander when a vacancy arose.

sentences.zh: 八年，克秣陵關，授直隸通永鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took Muling Pass and was appointed regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he captured Muling Pass and was appointed regional commander of the Tongyong garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時江寧長圍漸合，賊百計潰圍，屢出衝突。

translations.literal: At that time the long encirclement of Jiangning was gradually closing; the rebels tried every stratagem to break out and repeatedly sallied forth in assault.
translations.idiomatic: By then the long encirclement of Jiangning was slowly tightening; the rebels tried every means to break out and sallied forth again and again.

sentences.zh: 文英從張國樑四面兜剿，直抵外壕，焚毀望樓。

translations.literal: Wenying followed Zhang Guoliang in encircling and suppressing them on all four sides, pressed straight to the outer moat, and burned the watch towers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying followed Zhang Guoliang in encircling and suppressing them on all four sides, pressed to the outer moat, and burned the watch towers.

sentences.zh: 皖北援賊陷溧水，文英偕張玉良馳赴會剿，分攻紅藍埠，逼河砲擊，乘夜渡河，踏平賊壘，遂復溧水。

translations.literal: Relief rebels from northern Anhui took Lishui; Wenying, together with Zhang Yuliang, galloped to join the joint suppression, divided forces to attack Honglan Bu, pressed the river with cannon fire, crossed the river by night, overran the rebel stockades, and recovered Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: When relief rebels from northern Anhui took Lishui, Wenying and Zhang Yuliang raced to join the joint suppression, divided forces to attack Honglan Bu, shelled the river line, crossed by night, overran the rebel stockades, and retook Lishui.

sentences.zh: 而賊復自西路來援，文英自督前隊，以劈山砲迎擊，騎兵包抄，斃賊無算。

translations.literal: When the rebels again came to the relief from the western route, Wenying personally commanded the vanguard, met them with mountain-splitting cannon, and with cavalry enveloping them from the flanks killed rebels beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels again came to the relief from the west, Wenying personally led the vanguard, met them with mountain-splitting cannon, and with cavalry enveloping the flanks killed rebels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 會提督鄧紹良在寧國為賊所困，文英馳援，遇賊於灣沚，連戰皆捷，而賊至愈眾，力竭，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Just then the commandant Deng Shaoliang was besieged by rebels at Ningguo; Wenying galloped to the relief, met the rebels at Wanzhi, and won successive victories, but as the rebels grew ever more numerous his strength was spent and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Just then commandant Deng Shaoliang was besieged at Ningguo; Wenying raced to his aid, met the rebels at Wanzhi, and won victory after victory, but as enemy numbers swelled his strength gave out and he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 文英在軍中以善戰名，為張國樑所倚，甫擢專閫而殞。

translations.literal: Wenying was known in the army for skill in battle and was relied upon by Zhang Guoliang; he had just been promoted to independent command when he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying was famed in the army for fighting skill and was one on whom Zhang Guoliang relied; he had just been raised to independent command when he fell.

sentences.zh: 文宗惜之，優詔賜卹，稱其所向有功，克溧水，破援賊，功為尤著，予騎都尉世職，諡武烈。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong mourned him; a favorable edict granted posthumous honors, declaring that wherever he had been sent he had achieved merit, that in taking Lishui and breaking the relief rebels his service was especially outstanding; he was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant and given the posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong mourned him; a favorable edict granted posthumous honors, declaring that wherever he had been sent he had achieved merit, that in taking Lishui and breaking the relief rebels his service was especially outstanding; he was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant and honored with the posthumous title Martial and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 論曰：烏蘭泰忠勇冠軍，與向榮不合，致無成功，時論多右之。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: Wu Lantai's loyalty and courage stood foremost in the army; he did not agree with Xiang Rong, so success was never achieved, yet contemporary opinion largely sided with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: Wu Lantai's loyalty and courage stood foremost in the army; he and Xiang Rong could not work together, so success eluded him, yet opinion at the time largely favored him.

sentences.zh: 鄧紹良、週天受老於軍事，保障皖南，軍律不嚴，終不能保全浙境。

translations.literal: Deng Shaoliang and Zhou Tianshou were veterans of military affairs who secured southern Anhui, but because army discipline was not strict they ultimately could not preserve Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shaoliang and Zhou Tianshou were seasoned in war and held southern Anhui secure, but lax discipline in their armies kept them from saving Zhejiang in the end.

sentences.zh: 張玉良後起，號驍健，江南師潰之後，竟不復振。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang rose later, was famed for dash and strength, yet after the Jiangnan armies collapsed he never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang rose later and was famed for dash and strength, yet after the Jiangnan armies collapsed he never regained his footing.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆當一面，以死勤事，其成敗有足鑑者。

translations.literal: All these men held independent commands and died in loyal service; their success and failure offer lessons enough.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these men held an independent command and died in loyal service; their triumphs and failures are warning enough.

sentences.zh: 雙來、瞿騰龍、王國才、虎坤元、戴文英並以善戰名，志決身殲，時論惜焉。

translations.literal: Shuang Lai, Qu Tenglong, Wang Guocai, Hu Kunyuan, and Dai Wenying were all famed for skill in battle; resolved in will, they died to the last man, and contemporary opinion mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang Lai, Qu Tenglong, Wang Guocai, Hu Kunyuan, and Dai Wenying were all famed for fighting skill; resolute to the end, they died to the last man, and their contemporaries mourned them.
